findings.finding: `requirePerm` is a credential-shape gate, not an authorization gate: for a classic PAT or any browser session it evaluates no predicate and falls through to the handler
findings.status: fixed — every credential shape now passes both its credential grant and the target-resource authorization check; classic scopes, fine-grained selection/permissions/approval/expiry, and App/OAuth repository reach are regression-tested at the authorization chokepoint

findings.finding: `token.Scopes` is stored, persisted and emitted as `X-OAuth-Scopes` but enforced nowhere — a PAT scoped `read:org` can delete organizations
findings.status: fixed — the classic scope map was completed rather than partially enforced, and it defends itself three ways: `init()` panics at startup on a permission with no mapping, an AST test keeps `allPermScopes` in step with the const block, and behavioural tests cover the gate. Verified by reversion: neutralising `classicScopeCovers` fails the organization-deletion and unscoped-token tests, dropping a mapping panics with the permission named, and removing a scope from the enumeration is caught as drift

findings.finding: The entire `/_apis/` runner protocol has no authentication; `ghHeadersMiddleware` does not even run on it
findings.status: fixed — every `/_apis/` and `/twirp/` route carries one of `requireRunnerAuth`/`requireJobToken`/`requireAgentSession`/`requireRunnerSetupCredential`/`requireAssignedAgent`/`requirePlanJob`, except the five routes that necessarily authenticate inside their own handlers. Runner identity comes from an HMAC-signed registration token scoped to its owner, job endpoints bind the caller to the assigned agent or named plan, and regressions cover every decorator family plus the material acquire/renew/complete paths. AUTH-059 closed the jobs.go/run_service.go remainder this row previously described as open

findings.finding: Job messages carry every org/repo/environment secret in plaintext to any caller who can poll the broker
findings.status: fixed — `jobSecretsEntitled` gates entitlement and `pullPendingMessage` only hands a runner a message whose repository its registration scope covers. Unentitled *requests* 403 rather than returning a filtered message. Operator submissions name no repository and carry no secrets, so they stay deliverable — stated as a rule, not a fallthrough

findings.finding: Runtime tokens are `{"alg":"none"}` with an empty signature and a one-year expiry
findings.status: fixed — HS256 with a process key, TTL 365 days → 6h. `BLEEPHUB_RUNNER_TOKEN_KEY` pins it across replicas; otherwise 32 bytes from `crypto/rand` once per process, resolved at startup with a fatal on failure and no hardcoded default. Process-local is deliberate and matches the existing OIDC key: runner sessions are only meaningful against dispatch state that is itself process-local and cancelled on reload

findings.finding: `repoForRuntimeToken` trusts the unverified `sub` claim; forging a token is base64 encoding
findings.status: fixed — one `parseRunnerToken` checks `alg` and `hmac.Equal` **before** unmarshalling any claim; `jwtSubject` deleted. The old `repoForRuntimeToken` entry point is gone and its test rewritten to drive the live route, so the deadcode gate reports clean

findings.finding: Repository secret handlers never resolve the repo and never check admin; `PUT /repos/anything/at-all/actions/secrets/X` returns 201
findings.status: fixed — new `requireRepoAdmin` choke point applied at all six secret handlers and inside `resolveEnvScope`; 404 when unreadable or absent, 403 when readable but not admin. Deliberately redundant with `requirePerm`, and each handler was proved to deny on its own by invoking it directly

findings.finding: Case-variant paths write a shadow scope key the injector never reads: operator sets a production secret, gets 201, job runs without it
findings.status: fixed — every repository and environment secret handler keys off `repo.FullName`, the key the injector actually reads, never `owner+"/"+repo` from the path. A case-variant path resolves no repository and 404s instead of returning 201 into a scope nothing reads

findings.finding: `GET /internal/oauth/state` returns every live OAuth authorization code with its owning user ID to any authenticated caller — account takeover
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: 7 of 23 `/internal/` routes omit `requireSiteAdmin`, including every private repo's metadata and unmasked job logs
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: The CSRF token is set equal to the session cookie value and printed into the OAuth consent page HTML, defeating HttpOnly
findings.status: fixed — the CSRF token comes from its own generator rather than the cookie value, and the consent page mints a fresh token stored on the session which a successful POST rotates, making it single-use. The disclosure test needs *both* halves reverted to fail, which is why each half also has its own test

findings.finding: Branch protection is never consulted by either git transport; `branchProtectionForRepo` has no caller outside its own file
findings.status: fixed — HTTP, SSH and REST ref writes now share `protectedRefWriteRefusal`; it enforces push restrictions, creation/deletion/force-push allowances, required pull requests and checks, linear history and signed commits before a ref moves. A live transport regression protects `main`, then proves both `git push` over SSH and smart HTTP are refused and the remote ref stays put

findings.finding: `redirect_uri` is taken verbatim and never compared to the app's registered callback — authorization-code interception and open redirect
findings.status: fixed — exact match, or a sub-path of the registered callback at a segment boundary, with both sides `path.Clean`ed so `/cb/../../elsewhere` cannot prefix-match `/cb`. Enforced on the consent GET and inside the `completeAuthorize` choke point. See AUTH-063: GitHub Apps have no registered callback to compare against, so the flow now fails closed for them

findings.finding: Client secrets compared with `!=`, reachable unauthenticated and unrate-limited — byte-at-a-time timing oracle
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Every JWT verification failure is discarded and the request continues as anonymous; invalid `ghp_`/`gho_` tokens likewise
findings.status: fixed — a presented credential that does not verify is 401 rather than silently downgraded to anonymous, while no header at all stays anonymous. Verified by reversion: all seven credential shapes (`ghp_`/`gho_`/`ghu_`/`ghs_`/`ghr_`, an unverifiable JWT and free-form garbage) were admitted with the guard neutralised, and the no-header control stayed green

findings.finding: `browserLoginUser` accepts any PAT as a password with no scope check, laundering a restricted credential into an unrestricted session
findings.status: fixed — ordinary users authenticate browser sessions only with their local password or external identity; the sole token-form exception is an exact constant-time match for the configured bootstrap administrator token, and a regression proves even a scoped administrator PAT cannot become an unrestricted cookie

findings.finding: Public repo + GET bypasses scope, resource-owner and repository-selection checks — a PAT scoped to org A reads org B's Actions variable values
findings.status: fixed — both fine-grained-PAT carve-outs and the installation carve-out are keyed on the scope

findings.finding: Secret plaintexts and the X25519 private key that opens them are written unencrypted into adjacent rows of the same table
findings.status: fixed — the persistence boundary AES-256-GCM encrypts every Actions, Codespaces, App/OAuth, token, and browser-session credential row with bucket/key associated data; startup transactionally migrates plaintext rows and validates every envelope, while Terraform generates a retained 32-byte key in Secrets Manager and injects it only as an ECS secret

findings.finding: PATs are stored keyed *by* the raw token value; one DB read is total credential compromise
findings.status: fixed — PAT JSON never contains the one-time value, persisted lookup keys are SHA-256 digests, legacy raw-key rows migrate transactionally, and installation/OAuth/refresh/session bearer keys are independently replaced by HMAC digests derived from the persistence key

findings.finding: No `::add-mask::` handling and no log scrubbing anywhere — a secret echoed by a job is readable by any authenticated user
findings.status: fixed — every secret variable in a dispatched message is registered as a server-side plan mask, both `::add-mask::` and runner `##[add-mask]` commands extend it, and console plus uploaded log bytes are scrubbed before structured logging, in-memory storage, or object-store persistence

findings.finding: External identities are keyed on the mutable provider username, not `(issuer, subject)`; `SiteAdmin` is overwritten by whichever provider logged in last
findings.status: fixed — external identities now keyed on `(issuer, subject)` via `UsersByExternalID`; `SiteAdmin` is never overwritten on existing accounts by login

findings.finding: Any active org member gets push to every repo in the org regardless of role, team or base permission
findings.status: fixed — read, push, and admin now share one locked capability lattice: the org's `default_repository_permission` (unset = read), active owner role, team grant, and collaborator grant are compared at their actual levels; matrix regressions cover none/read/write/admin

findings.finding: Nonexistent repo returns 404, existing-but-unauthorized returns 401 — a private-repository existence oracle
findings.status: fixed — authentication now precedes repository resolution: anonymous requests get a 401 challenge (required by the git HTTP protocol) whether or not the repo exists; authenticated-but-unauthorized requests get 404, indistinguishable from a nonexistent repo

findings.finding: Receive-pack errors matched by `strings.Contains(err, "EOF")`, then post-push hooks and workflow triggers fire for refs never written
findings.status: fixed — neither transport treats an error string containing `EOF` as success. The shared receive-pack path retains the per-ref report, and post-push work receives only commands whose status is `ok`, so a refused or failed ref raises no push event

findings.finding: SSH listener spawns an unbounded goroutine per connection with no handshake deadline and no cap
findings.status: fixed — the listener owns a 64-slot connection semaphore, bounds the handshake with a ten-second deadline, and serves each accepted channel inline so a client cannot fan out unbounded session goroutines

findings.finding: Read deadline cleared after the banner check so an idle connection holds one of 32 slots forever; limiter map never evicted
findings.status: fixed — proxied connections carry an activity-renewed idle deadline for their complete lifetime, and rate-limit identities are evicted after their window rather than accumulating forever; focused tests cover both

findings.finding: No rate limiting on any auth endpoint; the `X-RateLimit-*` headers are hardcoded constants
findings.status: fixed — REST and GraphQL requests consume credential/resource-scoped primary windows with live headers and the 60-request anonymous core budget, and the credential-verifying auth-flow endpoints (`/login`, `/auth/local`, `/auth/token`) now consume a per-IP per-minute `auth` budget, refusing over-budget attempts with GitHub's 403+`Retry-After` shape (device/OAuth token-exchange endpoints are excluded because they legitimately poll and carry their own slow_down). Production auth arrives through the reverse proxy, which tags `X-Forwarded-For`, so callers are limited by their real client IP; a direct loopback peer carrying no forwarded client (local binary/dev/e2e) is exempt. GitHub's separate secondary/abuse-detection limits are a distinct mechanism, out of scope for this finding. Regression: TestAuthFlowRateLimitBlocksBruteForcePerIP

findings.finding: Logins accepted with no allowlist, no case folding, no NFKC and no confusable check — `Alice`, `alice` and Cyrillic `аlice` are three accounts
findings.status: fixed — NFKC normalization and case folding applied; Latin/Cyrillic mixing rejected; `BLEEPHUB_ALLOWED_LOGINS` env var enforces a login allowlist; user creation and external login normalized

findings.finding: Runner registration is unauthenticated and mints a "management token" that is never stored or checked
findings.status: fixed — every registration/removal-token minting endpoint (repo/org/enterprise) is gated on `administration:write` or enterprise ownership, and the minted token is an HMAC-signed blob carrying its scope, purpose and ~1h expiry, so it needs no server-side registry; `handleRunnerRegistration` and `handleRegisterAgent` both verify that setup credential (`runnerSetupCredential`) before acting, and its purpose must match the runner_event. Closed alongside the AUTH-003/059 runner-auth chokepoint; regression: TestRunnerProtocolRejectsUnauthenticatedCalls plus the registration-token gating tests

findings.finding: The OAuth client secret is reused as the HMAC key for the state cookie
findings.status: fixed — a dedicated 32-byte CSPRNG key is generated at startup and used for state-cookie HMAC; the client secret is no longer reused as a cryptographic key

findings.finding: Logout Origin check is conditional on Shauth being configured, and `/ui/signed-out` destroys the session on a plain GET
findings.status: fixed — logout always validates Origin when the header is present; session destruction requires POST; GET renders the page without side effects

findings.finding: `Secure` inferred from a string prefix, copy-pasted at five sites, no `__Host-` prefix
findings.status: fixed — `isSecureRequest` checks `r.TLS` or `X-Forwarded-Proto`; session cookies get `__Host-` prefix when Secure; all five copy-pasted sites use the shared helper

findings.finding: CSRF token compared with `!=` while `identity.go:446` correctly uses `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: `mustAtoi` cannot fail; discards both `Sscanf` returns and yields 0 — a latent fail-open in the SSH auth path
findings.status: fixed — `parseGitSSHUserID` checks both `Sscanf` returns and returns an error; the caller drops the connection on parse failure (fail closed)

findings.finding: SSH key lookup re-parses every registered key per attempt under RLock; unparseable keys silently skipped; no `MaxAuthTries`
findings.status: fixed — parsed keys cached at registration and persistence load; lookup compares cached wire encodings; `MaxAuthTries: 6` enforced per connection

findings.finding: Repo secret delete discards the existence result, returns 204 for a secret that never existed, and writes a forged audit event
findings.status: fixed — delete returns 404 when the secret never existed; audit event only written when it did

findings.finding: Login never invalidates the presented session; no rotation on privilege change, so a demoted admin keeps admin for 12h
findings.status: fixed — successful login invalidates the presented session and mints a new one, preventing session fixation

findings.finding: Front-channel logout page sets `frame-ancestors *` on a GET with a session-destroying side effect
findings.status: fixed — CSP `frame-ancestors` limited to 'self' plus the configured Shauth issuer origin (the OP frames this endpoint during front-channel logout); revocation demands an exact issuer match and a non-empty OP `sid`, which a cross-site attacker cannot guess. The earlier POST-only gate broke the spec's GET-in-iframe delivery and left witness sessions alive (issue #112), so it is gone

findings.finding: Five-line comment defending a one-line assignment, arguing which provider string becomes the account key instead of not using one
findings.status: fixed — removed the comment

findings.finding: `installationRequestCanAccessRepo` fed one caller-chosen repo to `filterReposBySelection`, which is written for listing an installation's own repos and so has no owner check and treats non-`selected` as "allow everything handed to it" — an installation on the attacker's own account downloaded any private repository's CodeQL database
findings.status: fixed — routed through `installationCovers`

findings.finding: `viewerCanReadRepo` had no user-to-server arm, so a `ghu_` token was indistinguishable from a session on handler-gated routes and borrowed the bearer's collaborator access to repositories the app was never installed on — strictly broader than the `ghs_` token of the same app
findings.status: fixed — `canReadRepo` renamed `canReadRepoAsUser` across 30 files and 49 of 52 repo call sites routed through `viewerCanReadRepo`, whose signature moved to `context.Context` so the three GraphQL resolver families can reach it at all. The 3 unconverted sites sit inside the allowlisted RBAC layer and each is named. Pre-fix: all 5 cited routes returned 200 for a zero-installation `ghu_` where `ghs_` got 404

findings.finding: 17 handler-side `ReposByName` map reads remain unlocked; a concurrent map read/write is a fatal error the recovery middleware cannot catch, so this is a remote denial of service
findings.status: fixed — the remaining alert, package, workflow and payload readers resolve through `GetRepoByFullName`; existing one-off lock wrappers use it too. The environment lookup is explicitly `protectedEnvironmentLocked` because dispatch already owns `store.mu` — converting it to the locking accessor was rejected by the full-suite deadlock regression. A bounded create/delete-versus-lookup test runs under `-race`, and an AST ratchet rejects any new `s.store.ReposByName` read unless the same function visibly holds `s.store.mu` (with the two deliberately lock-owned helpers named)

findings.finding: Org hook delivery reads `hook.URL` on a delivery goroutine while `UpdateOrgHook` writes it; reproduces under `-race` on main and is missed by the CI race job's `-run` subset
findings.status: fixed — enqueue and redelivery already take a locked configuration snapshot; repository and organization hook getters/listers now also deep-copy the `Events` slice and `LastResponse`, so API rendering cannot retain a live store pointer either. A concurrent update/read regression validates both hook families under `-race` and mutates the returned slice to prove it is detached

findings.finding: `orgHookGate` checks only `canAdminOrg`, so the 11 handler-gated org-hook routes never reach `userToServerReachesOrg` — a `ghu_` token for an app installed nowhere `POST`s an org webhook pointing at an attacker URL (201) and lists them (200), while the same app's `ghs_` gets 404. Persistent exfiltration of every organization event. Same shape on `GET /orgs/{org}/installations` (ghu 200 / ghs 403)
findings.status: fixed — one org predicate `viewerHoldsOrgRole` with `viewerCanAdminOrg`/`viewerIsOrgMember` over it; `canAdminOrg`/`isActiveOrgMember` renamed to `…AsUser` and all caller-entitlement sites converted, including the eight follow-ups audited under AUTH-079. Pre-fix the planted webhook was created (201), listed (200) and left in the store

findings.finding: `TestPublicRepositoryBypassIsKeyedOnTheScope` passes on the pre-fix code, so the only regression test written for the fine-grained-PAT bypass cannot see the bug it names: it probes `scopeSecrets`, which `resourceCapabilityFor` promotes to `permAdmin`, so the resource gate refuses the outsider before the carve-out is reached. The underlying fix is real — `/actions/permissions` discriminates 200 pre-fix vs 403 at HEAD
findings.status: fixed — the three `/actions/permissions*` probes added; verified 3 failures on a pristine tree with both carve-outs reverted, and green at HEAD

findings.finding: Anonymous callers still read private-repo data on `/actions/artifacts`, `/actions/cache/usage`, `/actions/caches`, `/actions/oidc/customization/sub`, `/comments/{id}/reactions`, `/private-vulnerability-reporting` and `/stargazers`
findings.status: fixed — the original seven and the two routes found during remediation now deny private-repository callers without read access. Vulnerability-reporting status and stargazers use the credential-aware metadata-read predicate; the repository package list no longer turns a failed predicate into an implicit empty 200. Repository-installation discovery was corrected at the stronger boundary: it accepts only the authenticated app's JWT, filters by that app before returning an installation and honours selected-repository coverage. The read-matrix regression now drives both anonymous and unrelated classic-PAT callers and keeps positive controls for all three ordinary metadata routes

findings.finding: `/collaborators` is registered under `scopeContents` while `fineGrainedPATPermissionForPattern` maps it to `scopeAdministration`; both disagree with GitHub's documented `metadata:read` permission for collaborator reads
findings.status: fixed — every collaborator GET route and the fine-grained PAT classifier now use `metadata:read`, while collaborator mutations retain `administration:write`; an installation-token regression covers the documented read grant

findings.finding: `principalMayAccessTarget` ends in `return true`, so when the path names a repository that does not resolve the whole gate passes. Any handler that does not itself resolve the repo then acts on a caller-fabricated repo key — proven on repo webhooks (201 and a working hook) and Dependabot public keys (200 with the instance key). The org arm has the same shape: `if org := GetOrg(login); org != nil && !canAdminOrg(...)` skips the check for an org that does not exist, and `fineGrainedPATResourceAllowed` returns true on `repo == nil`. The path values distinguish named-but-absent from not-named, so this is fixable without over-blocking the routes that name no repository
findings.status: fixed in the predicate rather than per handler — `credentialMayAccessTarget` returns a three-valued verdict so named-but-absent gets its own answer, always 404 rather than the level-dependent 403. The org arm's `org != nil && !canAdminOrg(...)` and `fineGrainedPATResourceAllowed`'s `repo == nil → true` are both corrected. Pre-fix a route-table sweep found **38** routes serving a fabricated repository, including `POST .../actions/runners/registration-token` returning 201 with a usable token

findings.finding: Deliveries read the shared `*Webhook` while `UpdateHook`/`UpdateOrgHook` mutated it in place
findings.status: fixed — `Store.SnapshotHook` copies the config under the store lock at enqueue, so a delivery is signed by the config as of when it was queued

findings.finding: `insecure_ssl=1` was accepted, stored and echoed but never affected TLS — a silent no-op on a client-observable security setting
findings.status: fixed — selects a non-verifying client, as on GitHub

findings.finding: Three handlers had no repository gate at all and served a stranger against a private repo: `handleRepoArtifacts`, `handleOIDCCustomSubGet` and `handleListReactions` (all five of its registrations are repo-scoped)
findings.status: fixed — all three now call `enforceRepoReadable`

findings.finding: `enforceRepoReadable`, used by 10 callers, returned **true** for a repository that does not exist, so `/actions/runs` and `/actions/concurrency_groups` answered 200 for a fabricated repo while answering 404 for a real private one — an existence oracle running backwards
findings.status: fixed — not-named passes, named-but-absent 404, private-unreadable 404

findings.finding: `git-receive-pack` gated on `canPushRepo(user)` with no credential intersection, and sits entirely outside `requirePerm`
findings.status: fixed — new `viewerCanPushRepo` mirroring the read choke point, applied at both push gates

findings.finding: `/actions/caches` and `/actions/cache/usage` return 200 for a repository that does not exist and leak a private repository's `full_name` to a stranger; they are the two remaining entries in the sweep's exclusion list
findings.status: fixed — both reads now pass through `enforceRepoReadable`, giving named-but-absent and unreadable private repositories the same 404 behavior as the rest of the Actions surface

findings.finding: `canReadRepoLocked` is the same credential-blind class as AUTH-042 at 10 sites, but under `st.mu`: `viewerCanReadRepo` calls store methods that take `RLock`, so routing it there as-is risks deadlock. Needs `…Locked` variants of `ListAppInstallations`/`GetInstallation` first. Not covered by the AST guard
findings.status: fixed — aggregate issue and notification rows are gathered under the store lock, released, then filtered through a required credential-aware callback; nil exposes nothing. Thread reads use the same path, selected-repository App-token regressions cover both aggregate APIs, and the AST ratchet now bans the locked predicate outside RBAC

findings.finding: `canPushRepo`/`canAdminRepo` have no credential-aware choke point and no AST guard. `requirePerm` covers every `/api` route registered through it, so exposure is limited to plain `s.route` write handlers, but the class is explicitly **not** closed
findings.status: fixed — the write half is now closed the same way the read half is: `canPushRepo`/`canAdminRepo` are entries in the `userScopedPredicates` AST guard (`authz_chokepoint_test.go:54-55`), and `TestOnlyTheRBACLayerAsksWhetherAUserCanReadARepo` fails the build if any non-test file except `rbac.go`/`gh_apps_perms.go` references them. Grep confirms those two exempted files are the only remaining callers, so no plain-route write handler self-gates on a user-scoped predicate — the credential-intersecting `viewer*` helpers are the only path. The behavioural counterpart is AUTH-081's full repo-write ghu/ghs sweep

findings.finding: `canAdminOrgAsUser` dereferenced `user` and `org` with no nil check — a latent panic
findings.status: fixed — guarded

findings.finding: The `/_apis/` routes registered in these two files are still unauthenticated: `AgentRequest` acquire/update/complete, `FinishJob`, `ActionDownloadInfo`, the task routes and `plans/{planId}/events`. Unauthenticated job acquire and complete means anyone can take or finish another runner's work. The decorator family to apply already exists in auth.go
findings.status: fixed — all 8 routes gated, no allowlist entry added. Two new decorators in the existing family: `requireAssignedAgent` (agent session **plus** `job.AgentID == caller`) and `requirePlanJob` (job token **plus** the plan's scope matching the verified `sub`). Verified against the *plausible-but-wrong* choice, not merely against no gate: with `requireAgentSession` alone a runner registered for one repository read, renewed and completed another's job; with `requirePlanScope` alone one repository's job token completed another's, and on the `{planId}`-only path it refused the legitimate owner outright

findings.finding: `handleUpdateAgent` accepted an `authorization` block from the request body, letting a runner overwrite its own clientId and therefore its own scope — self-service privilege escalation
findings.status: fixed — the stored authorization is always preserved

findings.finding: The agent get/update/delete/list handlers were fleet-wide for any caller, and `handleCreateSession` synthesized a fake agent from the request body when lookup failed
findings.status: fixed — scoped via `callerSeesAgent`, 404 rather than 403 so ids are not probeable; the session now uses the authenticated agent

findings.finding: Registration, removal and JIT routes minted credentials for a repository or organization that does not exist, and a removal token could be replayed to register a runner
findings.status: fixed — 404 on an absent target, and removal tokens carry a distinct purpose

findings.finding: Validating `redirect_uri` correctly closed an open redirect but left GitHub Apps unable to complete the OAuth web flow at all: the `App` struct stores no callback URL — only `OAuthApp` does — so there is nothing to compare against and the check fails closed with `redirect_uri_mismatch`. Failing closed is the right posture, but a real GitHub feature is now refused. Needs a `CallbackURL` on `App` plus the manifest and registration plumbing
findings.status: fixed — `App.CallbackURL` in the same single-string shape `OAuthApp` already carries, so the authorize gate consults one field rather than two mechanisms. Validated (absolute, http/https, non-empty host) at the OAuth-App boundary, the manifest boundary and as a store-level backstop. A manifest naming more than one callback is **refused** rather than quietly reduced to the first. The hole is not reintroduced: an app with no registered callback still fails closed, covered for both store-created and manifest-created apps. Persistence verified through the reload harness, and the test fails when the field is tagged `json:"-"`

findings.finding: Source import reuses `allowPrivateWebhookTargets` as its private-address opt-out; the field name is webhook-specific but it is now the instance's only such switch
findings.status: fixed — renamed `allowPrivateOutboundTargets` / `BLEEPHUB_ALLOW_PRIVATE_OUTBOUND_TARGETS`, since it now gates source import as well as webhook delivery. The retired variable is **refused at startup** rather than ignored: silently dropping an operator's opt-out would make their own loopback receivers start failing with nothing said. Deny-by-default unchanged, and the scheme rule stays outside the opt-out

findings.finding: `POST git/blobs`, `trees`, `commits`, `tags` and `refs` had no handler-level permission check at all
findings.status: fixed — all carry `requireRepoPush`

findings.finding: `handleGetRepoSecretsPublicKey` took `_ *http.Request` and so served the Actions public key for any path whatsoever
findings.status: fixed — resolves and gates

findings.finding: `handleFinishJob` and `handleJobEvents` fell back to a **body-supplied `jobId`** when the plan did not resolve, and then completed that job — a second path to finishing an arbitrary job, independent of the route gate, ending in a `warn + 200 {"status":"ok"}` silent no-op
findings.status: fixed — the job resolves from `{planId}` only; a body `jobId` may confirm it (400 on mismatch) but never select it, and an unresolvable plan is a loud 404

findings.finding: `requirePlanScope` binds the token to `{scopeId}` while `handleUpdateRecords` and `handleWebConsoleLog` act on `{planId}`, so a valid job token writes another job's timeline and console log — cross-tenant forgery of the output a human reads to judge whether a build is trustworthy. Demonstrated concretely on the sibling FinishJob route
findings.status: fixed — all eight timeline routes plus `ActionDownloadInfo` moved to `requirePlanJob`, and `requirePlanScope` is deleted since no correct caller remained. Verified against the plausible-but-wrong decorator: with `requirePlanScope` restored, one repository's job token forged a completed step and console output into another repository's plan, all 200

findings.finding: `repoForJobScope` requires a non-empty `github.repository`, which `buildJobMessage` sets to `""` for operator-submitted jobs, so those jobs' runtime tokens are rejected on every job-token route and such a job cannot report progress or completion at all. Pre-existing on the timeline routes
findings.status: fixed without needing `auth.go` — `repoForJobScope` now separates "no such plan" from "plan names no repository". Not a wildcard: every consumer of the scope was audited, and an operator token reaches its own plan (200) while another plan is 403 and every repository-scoped surface refuses it (cache 401, artifact 404)

findings.finding: An ephemeral runner is deregistered mid-teardown, so its final `DELETE AgentRequest` — and the `DELETE AgentSession` beside it — arrive after the agent is gone and take a 401, costing retries at teardown
findings.status: fixed — deregistration moved to `handleDeleteSession`, the runner's genuinely last call. Moving it to `DELETE AgentRequest` as first proposed would have fixed that route and broken the session delete after it; only this position covers both. Moving it later opened a window where a finished ephemeral runner could be handed a second job, closed by `agentTakesAJobLocked`. Residual, stated: a runner killed without deleting its session lingers as an inert offline registration, which is also what real GitHub does

findings.finding: A third instance of the plan-binding class, found by sweeping rather than by report: `POST /_apis/v1/Logfiles/{scopeId}/{hubName}/{planId}/{logId}` takes log ids from a single global counter with no owner recorded, so a job legitimately naming its own plan could upload into another plan's log container
findings.status: fixed — `claimLog` records the reserving plan, upload refuses any other, and deleting the data releases the claim so it cannot outlive the bytes

findings.finding: A session with no agent was accepted, and under `requireAssignedAgent` would receive a job it could never renew or complete — a silent dead end
findings.status: fixed — refused

findings.finding: The GraphQL mutation lane read through the credential-aware choke point and then asked only about the bearer for push and admin, so a `ghu_` token was strictly broader than the `ghs_` of the same app across 20 mutations — 15 at push including `mergePullRequest`, 5 at admin including `deleteRepository`. **A regression from the previous commit on the push half**: tightening only the `ghs_` side created the asymmetry. Reproduced on a *public* repository — on a private one the read gate refuses first and the write half is never reached, which is how a test of this passes while the hole is open
findings.status: fixed — each policy row now carries both the fine-grained scope the mutation is granted at and the standing the bearer needs, checked separately, so `ghs_` and `ghu_` reach the same answer and neither is broader than the other

findings.finding: `TestGitHubClassroomTransitionExportImportAndNoOperatorSeeds` is order-dependent and **panics** rather than failing (`interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not []interface {}`), aborting the package so every test scheduled after it silently never runs. Hit 3 times in 13 shuffled runs; identical at the previous commit, so pre-existing
findings.status: fixed — the test creates its own organization and classroom, verifies that exact classroom by name in the transition bundle, and no longer relies on an earlier test's fixture

findings.finding: The `/_apis/` allowlist is described as two entries; enumerating `routePatterns` shows five undecorated routes. The three extra (`Agent/{poolId}`, artifact download, cache by id) each authenticate inside the handler, so there is no hole — the description is wrong, and `TestRunnerProtocolRejectsUnauthenticatedCalls` is a hand-written list rather than a sweep of the route table
findings.status: fixed — comment now documents the full five-route allowlist; test rewritten as a sweep over routePatterns with a 30-route floor

findings.finding: dqlite inter-node transport has no authentication and no TLS, contradicting the "keeps the wire protocol private" claim
findings.status: fixed — the transport now runs over TLS 1.3 with a per-cluster identity derived from `BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_SECRET` (`dqliteaddr.TLSConfig`): the node wraps its listener with `tls.NewListener` and the dialer connects with `tls.Client` pinned to the secret-derived root, so a peer from another cluster's secret is rejected at the handshake. Authentication is a constant-time (`subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`) check of the secret header on the `/dqlite` HTTP upgrade, and `NewPersistence` refuses to start without the secret. Covered by `TestDqliteHTTPDialUpgrades` (presents the secret + upgrades over TLS), `TestDqliteHTTPDialRejectsUnupgradedResponses` (wrong-secret 401 rejected) and `TestDqliteHTTPDialRejectsAnotherClusterTLSIdentity` (cross-cluster TLS identity rejected)

findings.finding: The `viewerCan*` family answers only `installationReachesRepo` — whether an installation is **on** a repository — and never `hasPerm`, whether it is **entitled**. On `requirePerm` routes `hasPerm` runs first, so reaching is correctly half the answer; on the self-gating surfaces (`/api/graphql`, git smart-HTTP) nothing supplies the other half. **A regression from the previous commit**: the arm it replaced was `canAdminRepo(botUser, …)`, which refused by accident, so the fix swapped accidental blocking for unconditional admission. An app installed on the owner with only `metadata:read` deletes the repository through GraphQL (200) and clones and pushes a private repository over git (200/200, against 401/403 on main)
findings.status: fixed — installation, user-to-server, OAuth-App, classic PAT, and fine-grained PAT grants are intersected with repository reach on REST, GraphQL, and Git; deletion, clone/push, and organization-hook regressions cover the formerly open lanes

findings.finding: `authorMayAct` returns before the credential switch, and 16 of the 20 mutations carry it — four at admin level. On a public repository an author holding no push, through an app installed nowhere, retitled the issue with a `ghu_` where the same app's `ghs_` was refused. The author exemption must relax the user predicate *below* the credential intersection, not above it
findings.status: fixed — the author exemption sits below `credentialGrantsRepo` and above `principalHoldsRepoCapability`, the only half authorship speaks to. Proved by reverting the ordering alone

findings.finding: The mechanical ratchet bans three read-side names and not `canPushRepo`/`canAdminRepo`, which is why it stayed green through the write-side regression it exists to prevent. Verified: reverting the GraphQL write arm leaves the test passing
findings.status: fixed — `canPushRepo` and `canAdminRepo` are on the ratchet, and the 63 direct callers that exposed were routed through the credential-aware family, each naming the scope its route family is granted at. `viewerMayActOnRepo` carries the grant and the standing separately for the handlers where they differ — a code-scanning alert is granted at `security_events:write` while this server demands repository admin of a human

findings.finding: The refusal is chosen by required level, so an unrelated authenticated caller gets 403 for an existing private repository and 404 for an absent one — an existence oracle across 15 routes. Both were 404 on main. AUTH-049's rule was applied to named-but-absent and not to present-but-invisible
findings.status: fixed — `denyResourceAccess` answers 404 whenever the caller cannot read the repository named in the path, whatever level the route asked for; 403 is reserved for a caller who can read it and merely lacks the standing to change it

findings.finding: Eight sites open-code `GetMembership(orgLogin, user.ID)` rather than `viewerIsOrgMember`; `GET /orgs/{org}/members` returns the non-public member list to a `ghu_` of an app installed nowhere. AUTH-045's 55-site conversion missed them
findings.status: fixed for seven; the eighth refuted — `gh_copilot.go:340` reads the *target* user’s membership, not the caller’s, so it is a data lookup and not a self-entitlement. The real defect in that handler is the credential-blind `caller.Login == username` arm, now intersected with `viewerReachesOrg`. The other seven go through `viewerIsOrgMember`, `viewerCanAdminOrg` or `viewerReachesOrg`; the two `/user/memberships/orgs/{org}` sites take the last because they must still return a *pending* invitation

findings.finding: `projectRule` and `viewerOnly` are credential-blind: `canWriteProjectV2` is `user.ID == owner.id` with no intersection, so a `ghu_` of an app installed nowhere created a ProjectV2 where its `ghs_` was refused
findings.status: fixed — `canReadProjectV2` and `canWriteProjectV2` intersect `credentialGrantsAccount` over the owning account with the owner-scoped predicate. `viewerOnly` is gone: `createRepository` answers to `repoCreationRule`, which resolves the owner through the same helper the resolver creates under and demands `administration:write` over that account

findings.finding: AUTH-057 sized: sweeping all 244 plain-route repository writes found 8 asymmetric cells; `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets` returns 201 to a `ghu_` of an app installed nowhere and 404 to its `ghs_`
findings.status: fixed — the whole sweep is re-driven behaviourally: `TestNoRepoWriteServesAGhuBroaderThanItsGhs` iterates every registered mutating route under `/repos/{owner}/{repo}` (259 today) and asserts, against the victim's real private repository, that the outside app's `ghs_` is refused everywhere and its `ghu_` is never served where that `ghs_` is refused. No asymmetric cell remains: the named `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets` cell plus the whole self-gating class were routed through the credential-intersecting `viewer*` helpers (`gh_apps_perms.go`) by the earlier chokepoint sweep, and the AST ratchet `TestOnlyTheRBACLayerAsksWhetherAUserCanReadARepo` structurally forbids reintroducing a bearer-only gate

findings.finding: `viewerAdminsRepo` is a body-identical duplicate of `viewerCanAdminRepo`, differing only by a nil guard the newer one lacks — so the "one choke point" is two
findings.status: fixed — `viewerAdminsRepo` deleted; its two callers go through `viewerCanAdminRepo`, which keeps the nil guard

findings.finding: `authenticateRequest` reads a credential only from the `token` and `bearer` schemes, so `RemoteAuth` — the scheme actions/runner v2.321.0 presents its registration token with on `POST /api/v3/actions/runner-registration` — resolved to nothing and `ghHeadersMiddleware` answered "Bad credentials" before the handler ran. `runnerRegistrationCredential` accepted `remoteauth` and was unreachable for it. The real runner could not configure itself at all; every existing test of that route sent `Bearer`, which is why nothing saw it
findings.status: fixed — `runnerCredentialOffered` names the three schemes a runner credential may arrive under, and the runner-credential arm consults it rather than the user-credential variable. The harness was also passing a literal placeholder for `--token`, which the newly-authenticated route correctly refuses; it now mints a real one through `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners/registration-token`

findings.finding: Three routes `config.sh` reaches *before* an agent session exists were gated on one: `GET /_apis/v1/Agent/{poolId}` (the pool lookup of the runner's own name, which every configuration performs), `PUT …/{agentId}` (`--replace`) and `DELETE …/{agentId}` (`config.sh remove`). The runner holds only its registration or removal token there, so each answered 401. The removal token had no accepting route at all — `handleRunnerRegistration` verified every credential as a registration one and minted a registration token whatever `runner_event` asked for, so `config.sh remove` could not complete and a removal token could be exchanged for one that registers
findings.status: fixed — the config-time decorator takes the purposes a route accepts and puts the verified scope on the request as a principal with no agent, so `callerSeesAgent` confines it to its own tenant; `runner_event` selects the purpose the presented token must carry and the one minted back. A registration token cannot delete a runner and a removal token cannot add one

findings.finding: `handleUpdateAgent` restored the whole registration-time authorization, discarding the RSA public key the runner sent. `config.sh --replace` generates a fresh key pair and signs its next `client_assertion` with it, so a re-registered runner was left unable to obtain a session — 401 at `POST /_apis/v1/auth/` with a verification error
findings.status: fixed — the clientId and authorization URL stay server state; the public key is taken from the update

findings.finding: `runner_event` was parsed and then ignored: every presented credential was verified as a *registration* token and a registration token was minted back whatever the event said. So a removal token had no route anywhere that would accept it, and — the security half — a removal token could be exchanged for one that registers
findings.status: fixed — the event selects both the purpose the presented token must carry and the one minted back; a removal token cannot add or replace and a registration token cannot delete, each 401, and an unknown event is 400

findings.finding: The harness passed the literal string `BLEEPHUB_REG_TOKEN` where a token belonged — invisible while the route was unauthenticated — and its wait loop polled an endpoint anonymously, swallowed the failure for 30 seconds and then reported the runner missing
findings.status: fixed — mints a real token through the REST API and fails loudly

findings.finding: The agent's scope was encoded into `authorization.clientId` as a signed blob, on the stated assumption that "the runner treats the clientId as opaque". It does not — it deserializes that field into a `System.Guid`, so the real runner failed configuration outright with a type-conversion error. A fidelity break: a real protocol field must carry its real type
findings.status: fixed — the clientId is a bare GUID and the scope lives on the agent record, which `LookupAgentByClientID` already indexes. A GUID is guessable where a blob is not, and that is fine: the clientId only names whose public key to verify against, and the RSA `client_assertion` signature is what authenticates. The handshake test now asserts the clientId parses as a UUID, so the shape cannot regress into one the runner rejects

findings.finding: The runner harness discarded the evidence for its own failures: `config.sh` output went through `tail -5`, bleephub ran at `info` so the per-request log was never emitted, and the failure dump read only `Worker_*.log` — the job logs — while a configuration failure writes `Runner_*.log` and leaves the worker logs empty. A config failure therefore reported one line of context and nothing else
findings.status: fixed — full output kept and dumped on failure, debug level by default, and the config-time diagnostics included

findings.finding: The grant intersection is guarded on `uts.AppID != 0`, so `gho_` OAuth-App tokens — which carry classic scopes `userToServerHasPerm` already knows how to evaluate — skip it entirely, as do fine-grained PATs, whose repository selection is never consulted on the self-gating surfaces (`/api/graphql` has no `{repo}` in its pattern, so the fine-grained gate passes it through). Both were equally blind on main
findings.status: fixed — the `AppID != 0` guard is off the grant half of `credentialGrantsRepo`/`credentialGrantsAccount` and stays off the reach half, which is the asymmetry a `gho_` needs: its scopes are the whole of what it carries and it reaches no installation, so `userToServerReachesRepo`/`…Account` admit an AppID-less token by design. A fine-grained arm sits beside it (`fineGrainedPATGrantsRepo`/`…Account`), and `fineGrainedPATSelectsRepo` is now the one selection predicate the routed gate and the resolvers share. `classicOAuthScopesOffered` closes the same shape in `enforceFineGrainedPATResource`, which read a classic PAT's scopes and not a `gho_`'s — that was the org-webhook half. A credential × surface matrix against main moved 40 cells and every one of them tightened; the entitled controls (`gho_` holding the scope, fine-grained token selecting the repository, classic `repo` PAT, browser session, anonymous read of a public repository) are unchanged

findings.finding: The just-in-time config blob is emitted as nested objects; the runner deserializes it as `Dictionary<string,string>` where each key is a file name and each value is that file's base64 contents, so it fails outright. `.credentials_rsaparams` is also absent while the runner writes that file verbatim on the JIT path, and no public key is recorded, so `verifyAgentClientAssertion` answers "no registered public key". JIT ephemeral runners can neither configure nor obtain a session. `runner_setup_test.go:153` pins the broken shape
findings.status: fixed — the blob is a map of file name to base64 file contents, as the runner deserializes it, and carries `.credentials_rsaparams` with fixed-width RSA components (.NET rejects a `D` that is not the modulus length; Go trims leading zeros). The public half is recorded on the agent so the assertion verifies. The test that pinned the broken shape now asserts the contract and completes a real token exchange with the key from the blob

findings.finding: `TestEphemeralRunnerTeardownStaysAuthenticated` is order-dependent — 2 of 10 shuffled runs fail on `renew job request … 403 This job request belongs to another runner`, because `pollForMessage` only asserts the body *contains* `PipelineAgentJobRequest`, so a foreign test's queued message satisfies it. A regression from the commit that added it
findings.status: fixed — the test puts its uniquely labelled message first in the shared fixture and decodes the envelope to require both the exact message type and its own plan marker; ten shuffled repeated runs pass

findings.finding: `userToServerHasPerm` returns the verdict of the *first* installation it reaches rather than asking them all, so once an app is installed in more than one place a `ghu_` token's grant is decided by Go's map iteration order: 40 identical `git-upload-pack` requests answered 200 thirty-six times and 401 four times. The installation-narrowed branch has the same shape, returning on the first listed id. The reach half already scans every installation, so the two ranged over different sets and their intersection was neither
findings.status: fixed — both loops continue past a candidate that does not grant and answer true only when one does, which is what the reach half already did. Not a widening: an attacker could re-roll the old draw at will, so the union was already the reachable set. `TestUserToServerGrantIsNotDecidedByMapOrder` fails pre-fix on the disagreement itself

findings.finding: The same class as AUTH-090 for the third scope-bearing shape: a classic PAT's scope selection was read by `enforceFineGrainedPATResource` on routed handlers and by nothing on `/api/graphql` or the git transports, so a `ghp_` with **no scopes at all** cloned and pushed a private repository (200/200) and deleted one through `deleteRepository`. Not a regression — main was equally blind
findings.status: fixed — `credentialGrantsRepo` checks the selection on the same terms `classicScopeGateApplies` sets for the routed gate: writes only, because the classic scopes are coarse there while GitHub's read rules vary per endpoint and a wrong read denial turns into a 404 that hides a resource the caller may see. Reads and every scoped token are unchanged in the matrix

findings.finding: Two evasions leave the ratchet green: a function variable (`var f = canPushRepo; f(...)`) since the walk only matches a direct `*ast.Ident` callee, and `canReadRepoLocked` — a body-equivalent twin declared inside an allowlisted file and called from 10 sites elsewhere, which is the same duplicate-predicate class as `viewerAdminsRepo`. The second is live and already tracked as AUTH-056
findings.status: fixed — the ratchet scans every identifier reference rather than only direct call expressions, so aliases are caught, and the duplicate locked predicate was removed entirely

findings.finding: Federated login resolved a mutable `preferred_username` against `UsersByLogin` when no `(issuer,subject)` binding existed, then bound the attacker's identity to that account. A Shauth principal named `admin` (or a confusable that NFKC-folds to it) thereby seized the seeded SiteAdmin account — full instance takeover; the primitive claimed any local account
findings.status: fixed — `upsertExternalUser` resolves on `(issuer,subject)` first and requires a stable subject. The primary IdP may adopt a same-named LOCAL account (SSO taking ownership of the seeded bootstrap admin — the flow the shauth contract exercises), but privileges then come from the role claim, so a developer-role `admin` lands on a NON-SiteAdmin account and escalates nothing; a secondary provider, or an account already bound to a different federated identity, is refused. `TestUpsertExternalUserNeverEscalatesByUsername`

findings.finding: `BLEEPHUB_ALLOWED_LOGINS` was enforced only on local login; both SSO callbacks provisioned and authenticated any principal, silently voiding the operator's restriction
findings.status: fixed — `upsertExternalUser` consults `loginAllowed` before provisioning or resolving, so the allowlist governs the SSO paths too. `TestUpsertExternalUserHonorsAllowlistAndAuthoritativeRole`

findings.finding: The IdP `role` claim was applied only when creating an account; a later demotion or promotion at the provider never took effect, so de-provisioning failed open (a demoted admin kept SiteAdmin forever)
findings.status: fixed — the primary IdP (Shauth) writes SiteAdmin on every login; a secondary provider never writes it, so a second federated identity cannot reshape privileges (preserves AUTH-021). Same test

findings.finding: `POST /api/v3/authorizations` (and the `PATCH`) were plain routes gated only on `ghUserFromContext != nil`, so any bearer — a `gist`-only PAT, a `ghu_` of an app installed nowhere — minted itself an arbitrary-scope classic PAT, or rewrote its own scopes wider. A concurrent DELETE also nil-dereferenced under the store lock, deadlocking the server
findings.status: fixed — the authorizations API demands a browser session (password-equivalent authority) and refuses every derived bearer; the update/create paths re-check the credential under the write lock before dereferencing. `TestLegacyAuthorizationsRefuseBearerCredentials`

findings.finding: `GET /token` minted a signed Actions OIDC JWT from query parameters after checking only `user != nil`, so any authenticated principal (even a zero-scope PAT) forged a `sub` like `repo:victim/prod:environment:production` and defeated a cloud trust policy — cross-tenant credential takeover
findings.status: fixed — the route is gated on the per-job runtime token, and the mint refuses unless that token is scoped to the requested repository. `TestOIDCToken_RequiresJobTokenScopedToRepo`

findings.finding: `authenticateRequest` set `ctxUser` before the suspension check (a suspended `ghu_`/`gho_` kept git-HTTP and registry access), rejected `ghs_`/`ghu_`/`gho_` Basic passwords (the `x-access-token` convention), and fell back to the session cookie when a token was offered (a revoked token served as the cookie's user)
findings.status: fixed — a shared `resolveBearerCredential` handles every token shape without placing a suspended user on the context, Basic passwords resolve through the same switch, and the session is consulted only when no Authorization header was offered

findings.finding: Authorization resolved `(owner,repo)` with one `.git` trim while `storeLoader.Load` trimmed `.git` again, so a request to `owner/app.git.git` authorized against `owner/app.git` but streamed the private `owner/app` packfile (SSH shared the shape; receive-pack mixed two repos' storage)
findings.status: fixed — sessions are built from the already-authorized storer via a fixed loader, never re-derived from a string; repo creation rejects names with separators, whitespace, or a trailing `.git`. `TestCreateRepoRejectsAmbiguousNames`

findings.finding: The site-admin / enterprise-owner gates checked only `user.SiteAdmin`, and the fine-grained-PAT gate skipped patterns without `{repo}`/`{org}`. A site admin's fine-grained PAT, OAuth/App user token, installation token, or app JWT thereby administered the whole appliance (e.g. minting impersonation tokens for any account)
findings.status: fixed — the gates require a broad credential shape (browser session or classic PAT) via `credentialConveysSiteAdmin`. `TestGHESAdminSurfaceRejectsNarrowCredentials`

findings.finding: `GET/DELETE /user/keys/{id}` acted on any key by id: GET had no auth wrapper and no ownership check, DELETE checked no ownership, so any caller read or revoked any user's SSH key (locking them out of the SSH transport)
findings.status: fixed — both are owner-scoped, returning 404 for a key that is not the caller's (no read, no revoke, no existence oracle); GET requires a caller. `TestUserSSHKeyIsOwnerScoped`

findings.finding: Org SCIM bound a new record to any pre-existing global account by username and force-enrolled it, then `replace`/`patch` rewrote that account's global login/name/email — so an owner of one org took over or renamed any account instance-wide
findings.status: fixed — SCIM only creates or mutates accounts its own org provisioned (new `User.SCIMManagedByOrg`); a collision with an unmanaged account is a 409. `TestOrganizationSCIMCannotHijackExistingAccount`

findings.finding: `POST /login` redirected to a `return_to` validated only by a non-empty path, so `https://evil/x` and `//evil/x` were honored — an open redirect landing the just-authenticated victim on an attacker page
findings.status: fixed — the legacy PAT login (only reachable when Shauth is unconfigured) no longer redirects to a caller-supplied `return_to` at all; it renders the signed-in page. The Shauth flow's `return_to` stays sanitized by `safeIdentityReturnTo` and laundered through the signed state cookie

findings.finding: An OAuth authorize request with no `scope` silently minted a `repo read:org gist` token — full private-repo read/write the user consented to nothing for
findings.status: fixed — an omitted scope carries the minimal read-only grant, never a silent upgrade

findings.finding: The `hmac:v1:` row key under which a token or session was persisted was itself accepted as the credential: in-memory tokens were keyed raw at mint but by digest after restore, and the lookup passed an already-`hmac:v1:` value through. A leaked backup/replica/query-log of row keys was a credential compromise
findings.status: fixed — mint and restore both key by the digest, lookups always digest the presented value (never pass an `hmac:v1:` input through), and session Get/Delete pass the digested key to the persistence layer. `TestPersistedRowKeyIsNotACredential`

findings.finding: The unprefixed `_gh_sess` shadowed `__Host-_gh_sess`: after logout cleared only the `__Host-` name, a planted `_gh_sess` survived and the next request adopted it (logout bypass / fixation)
findings.status: fixed — over HTTPS only the `__Host-` cookie is honored, and logout/sign-out expire BOTH names and revoke both records. `TestSecureDeploymentIgnoresUnprefixedSessionCookie`

findings.finding: `GetLoginSession` returned the pointer it also stored in the map, so a caller rotating the CSRF token raced a locked reader (`-race` failure; torn CSRF token)
findings.status: fixed — it returns a distinct copy

findings.finding: Signing out of a locally- or token-authenticated session started a global RP-initiated logout, tearing down the user's shared Shauth SSO session used by every other relying party
findings.status: fixed — the global logout runs only when the current session was itself established through Shauth. `TestLogoutOfNonShauthSessionDoesNotStartGlobalLogout`

findings.finding: `orgIDGated` set `{org}` only inside the handler, after `requirePerm` had already run its (empty-target) org check, so any authenticated caller — even a zero-scope PAT — rewrote another organization's Actions cache policy
findings.status: fixed — it re-checks org-admin against the resolved `{org_id}`

findings.finding: The org-PAT-admin `ghu_` branch checked only that the app's installation held the scope, never that the token owner was an org owner, so any account that authorized a suitably-scoped app could approve or revoke the org's PAT grants
findings.status: fixed — the branch also requires `canAdminOrgAsUser`

findings.finding: The SSH transport ran outside recovery (a decoder panic crashed the whole process), leaked a private-repo existence oracle (distinct stderr for missing vs unreadable), and the anonymous upload-pack request body was uncapped (OOM)
findings.status: fixed — per-connection panic recovery, unreadable repos answered as not-found, and a bounded upload-pack negotiation body

findings.finding: Actions OIDC subject customization lived in one process-wide slice, so one repo's admin clobbered every tenant's `include_claim_keys` and an anonymous caller read the org configuration
findings.status: fixed — stored per repository/org; the org GET requires org membership. `TestOIDCCustomSubIsScopedPerRepository`

findings.finding: git HTTP sits outside `ghHeadersMiddleware`, so a presented-but-invalid credential was downgraded to anonymous and served a public repo 200 (a PAT-guessing oracle)
findings.status: fixed — `authorizeGitHTTP` returns 401 for an invalid credential. `TestGitHTTPInvalidCredentialIs401`

findings.finding: Every OpenID Connect discovery and token verification ran its outbound HTTP over `http.DefaultClient` with no timeout, so a slow or hung IdP pinned a goroutine and socket per request — an anonymous DoS/amplification on the unauthenticated `/auth/*` endpoints. The ID token `azp` was also unchecked (OIDC Core §3.1.3.7)
findings.status: fixed — a 10s-timeout client bounds every discovery/JWKS fetch, and `azp` is validated (reject multi-audience without azp; azp must equal this client)

findings.finding: Local login returned 403 for a disallowed login and 401 for a wrong password, letting an anonymous caller enumerate `BLEEPHUB_ALLOWED_LOGINS` membership from the status code
findings.status: fixed — both return the identical 401. `TestLocalLoginAllowlistRejectsLoginsNotListed`

findings.finding: The per-flow OAuth state cookie carried no cookie prefix, so a sibling-subdomain or network attacker could transplant a server-signed state cookie into the victim's jar and log the victim in as the attacker
findings.status: fixed — the state cookie carries the `__Host-` prefix (Secure, Path=/, no Domain) over HTTPS; plain-HTTP dev keeps the unprefixed name. The per-process HMAC key across replicas remains open

findings.finding: Anonymous clone counting recorded the remote host in an unbounded `Actors` map and re-serialized the whole bucket on every request, so a public-repo clone flood (or a large IPv6 range) was a persisted memory/disk sink
findings.status: fixed — the distinct-actor set is capped at 10k; clone counts keep incrementing past the cap

findings.finding: OIDC discovery/JWKS/token/end-session and the Pages deployment artifact fetch were the only server-initiated fetches not routed through the SSRF address gate, so a provider-controlled discovery document or artifact URL could reach an internal or cloud-metadata address
findings.status: fixed — both now use `newAddressCheckedHTTPTransport` (dial-time `Dialer.Control`); `oidcClientContext` became a `*Server` method to read `allowPrivateOutboundTargets`, and the shauth loopback-issuer browser harness sets `BLEEPHUB_ALLOW_PRIVATE_OUTBOUND_TARGETS=true`

findings.finding: Private repo contents, commits and README readable by an anonymous caller; `lookupReadableRepoFromPath` exists and is not used
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Branch, tag and ref listings for private repos likewise anonymous
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Labels and milestones for private repos anonymous — roadmap and security leakage
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: All 14 protection GETs anonymous
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Private build logs, artifact bytes and workflow inventory anonymous
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Private CI results anonymous
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Commit-author emails and large-file paths anonymous
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Any logged-in user can force-push or delete `refs/heads/main` on any repository
findings.status: fixed — every git-data write route carries `requireRepoPush`, and every ref create/update/delete goes through the same `protectedRefWriteRefusal` as both git transports. Force pushes and deletions require their explicit allowances, creations honour `block_creations`, restrictions bind users, teams and installation apps, and `enforce_admins` removes the administrator bypass

findings.finding: Any authenticated user installs a webhook on any private repo and exfiltrates every subsequent payload
findings.status: fixed — the original existing-private-repository claim was refuted because every route already carried admin-promoted `scopeAdministration`. A worse unresolved-resource hole was fixed: a fabricated repository path could create a working hook because no handler resolved the repository. One `hookRepo` helper covers all 12 handlers and unknown-hook 404 precedes body validation

findings.finding: All 41 branch-protection routes unauthorized — privilege escalation against the merge gate in the same file
findings.status: fixed — all 12 previously ungated GET routes now carry `requirePerm(scopeAdministration, permRead)`, matching the 29 sibling write routes; the scope is admin-promoted

findings.finding: 13 Dependabot secret handlers with no collaborator or admin check
findings.status: fixed — the no-admin claim was refuted because all 16 routes already carried admin-promoted `scopeDependabotSecrets`. The two public-key handlers did have an unresolved-resource hole and returned the instance key for a nonexistent repository; both now resolve and authorize the target

findings.finding: Installation repository allowlist mutable by any user on an arbitrary installation ID; `user` is resolved and never used
findings.status: fixed — list/add/remove bind the installation to the user account or active org membership/owner, bind `ghu_` credentials to their app and optional installation subset, require selected mode, validate repository ownership/type, and revalidate mode + ownership atomically in the Store

findings.finding: Map write performed under a read lock — `fatal error: concurrent map writes`, unrecoverable
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Eight unsynchronized reads of maps written under the write lock — `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`
findings.status: fixed — every verified unlocked access now goes through a locked Store method, including the final OAuth client lookup. The six apparent remnants were audited in context and already execute while holding the Store lock. A concurrent lookup/mutation regression covers the last conversion

findings.finding: Live store pointers rendered outside the lock; `populateGistURLs` writes a request-derived base URL into the shared object on every GET
findings.status: fixed — response-facing reads across gists, codespaces, branch protection, comments, migrations, rulesets, GitHub Apps, installations and installation/user tokens now return detached snapshots; nested maps/slices/interfaces are deep-copied. Gist URLs are derived only onto the copy. Race and ownership regressions mutate returned objects while proving neither torn state nor request hosts reach stored state

findings.finding: Every unrecognized search qualifier is silently discarded, returning the unfiltered universe with `incomplete_results: false`
findings.status: fixed — `parseSearchQuery` returns an error and every handler goes through `searchQueryOrError`, which writes GitHub's 422 naming the qualifier. `state:` and `type:` were silently accepting garbage too, and a bogus `type:` disabled the user/org filter — the same disclosure shape as `is:`

findings.finding: Search results gathered by ranging a Go map and never ordered before slicing — pages overlap and omit nondeterministically
findings.status: fixed — `searchEnvelope` is the only pagination path and orders unconditionally before slicing (score desc, then id asc, then a unique string). Issue and PR ids come from separate counters so id alone is not total. Repo scans in code/commit search ordered too, since the 1000-result cap otherwise truncated a different subset each request

findings.finding: Check runs readable and PATCHable across tenants by integer guess; the sibling rerequest handler checks correctly
findings.status: fixed — `checkRunInRepo`/`checkSuiteInRepo` choke points applied to 5 handlers; the two rerequest handlers now call them instead of open-coding the rule. `handleGetCheckSuite` and `handleListCheckRunsForSuite` were cross-tenant readable too and were outside the reported range

findings.finding: Any deployment status readable through any repo path
findings.status: fixed — resolves `{deployment_id}`, asserts `d.RepoID == repo.ID` via the new `requireRepoOwns`, then asserts `status.DeploymentID == d.ID`; both foreign-deployment and foreign-status shapes covered

findings.finding: Any PR review comment readable, editable and deletable; the delete handler never resolves the repo
findings.status: fixed — `prReviewCommentInRepo` walks comment → PR → repo and 404s on mismatch across get/update/delete, delete resolves the repository, and authors may edit/delete their own comments without acquiring push while non-authors still require push

findings.finding: Any issue comment rewritable or deletable; `editorID` is recorded but not enforced
findings.status: fixed — repository binding is backed by the locked `Store.CommentRepoID`; authors may edit/delete their own comments without push and non-authors still require push

findings.finding: `PUT /contents` decodes `sha` and never reads it — every write is an unconditional overwrite, last writer silently wins
findings.status: fixed — `contentSHAPreconditionMet` enforces the `sha` precondition; a stale one is 409 and creating a new file requires it absent

findings.finding: Source import fetches an arbitrary URL synchronously in the request goroutine with no scheme allowlist, no IP filtering and no timeout
findings.status: fixed — the URL and every redirect use the shared outbound-target policy, the fetch has a five-minute deadline and runs off the request goroutine, and isolated per-import go-git protocols install a transport whose dial callback re-resolves and rejects every private address at connection time. A DNS-rebinding regression proves the dialed address is checked

findings.finding: `GET /users/{username}/codespaces` is invented, unauthenticated, and enumerates another user's codespaces
findings.status: fixed — the invented route and its handler are deleted. Verified nothing depends on it: the two remaining references are a fuzz vocabulary entry (an unregistered pattern just draws 404s) and an inert skip-set key, both in test files owned by others

findings.finding: Six gist sub-resource handlers skip the visibility check; `GET /gists/{id}/{sha}` returns full secret-gist contents to anonymous callers
findings.status: fixed — new `visibleGist`/`viewerCanSeeGist` choke point applied to all 14 by-id gist routes, not the six reported: get, revision, commits, forks, the five comment routes, star/unstar/check-starred, fork, update and delete

findings.finding: `userToJSON` has no nil guard and is called with a deleted user — confirmed nil dereference
findings.status: fixed — `userToJSON(nil)` normalizes to the real ghost account at the choke point, covering ~100 call sites; `fullUserJSON` guarded too (it dereferenced `u.Bio` first). Two divergent hand-rolled ghosts deduped onto it, one of which emitted a wrong id 0

findings.finding: `col` guarded on one line and dereferenced twice on the next
findings.status: fixed — `projectCardToJSON` returns `(map, bool)`; a card whose column vanished is unrenderable rather than a nil-URL fabrication. List skips, the other three 404

findings.finding: Mutators return nil on concurrent delete and the caller dereferences unconditionally
findings.status: fixed — one generic `mutated[T any](w, *T) bool` guard at the choke point across all three, plus the nil guard missing inside `SetCodeSecurityConfigurationAsDefault`, which panicked for any unknown id and not only under a race

findings.finding: Pull requests are invisible in the issues list and in `GET /issues/{number}`; `issueToJSON` has no `pull_request` key
findings.status: fixed — `issueToJSON` carries the `pull_request` member, so pull requests appear in the issues list and in `GET /issues/{number}` as they do on GitHub

findings.finding: `&json.UnmarshalTypeError{Type: nil}` — confirmed by execution to panic the moment anything formats it
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: One `ETag` in 117 files and it is never honored; no `If-None-Match`, no 304, no `X-Poll-Interval`, no `X-GitHub-Media-Type`
findings.status: fixed — every successful JSON GET receives a strong body-derived ETag at the shared response choke point and `If-None-Match` (including weak and wildcard forms) returns a bodyless 304; `X-GitHub-Media-Type` is emitted globally. The activity event feeds and notifications list advertise `X-Poll-Interval: 60` (path-scoped at the shared header writer, excluding the issues-events list), and binary release-asset downloads are conditional — a stable `"asset-<id>-<size>"` ETag with `If-None-Match` returning a bodyless 304 that is not counted as a download. All activity-event feeds (public/user/org/received/repo/network) and the notifications lists now advertise `Last-Modified` from their newest entry and honor `If-Modified-Since` with a bodyless 304, ignoring it when an `If-None-Match` is present per RFC 7232 §3.3

findings.finding: `ghResponseWriter` erases `Flusher`/`Hijacker`, so the downstream `Flush()` is a silent no-op
findings.status: fixed — the wrapper exposes `Unwrap`, `Flush`, and `Hijack` through `http.ResponseController`, preserving streaming and upgrade behavior while still committing GitHub headers first

findings.finding: `page=abc`, `page=0`, `per_page=-1` silently become defaults
findings.status: fixed — the REST middleware rejects malformed and non-positive pagination before a handler can reinterpret it as a default; the shared slicer retains GitHub's 100-item ceiling

findings.finding: `Link` header URLs are relative; GitHub emits absolute
findings.status: fixed — the shared Link builder emits absolute targets and honors the first forwarded scheme/host supplied by a trusted deployment proxy

findings.finding: Truncate-only pagination ignores `page` entirely — page 2 is unreachable
findings.status: fixed — organization configurations use the shared overflow-safe page slicer and emit followable Link headers

findings.finding: `strconv.Atoi` on an opaque base64 cursor, error discarded — returns page 1 forever
findings.status: fixed — enterprise code-security lists decode opaque base64 `cursor:<id>` values (plus the former decimal form for compatibility) and reject malformed cursors with 422

findings.finding: Open-coded slicing drops the overflow guard — large `page` yields a negative index and a slice-bounds panic
findings.status: fixed — the repository-access envelope delegates its nested list to the shared int64 overflow-safe paginator

findings.finding: List endpoints return whole collections with no pagination and no `Link`
findings.status: fixed — a spec-driven AST ratchet (`TestGitHubPaginatedRoutesPaginate`) cross-references every registered GET route against the vendored OpenAPI description's `per_page` declarations and fails when a handler cannot reach a pagination primitive transitively; the 69 routes it caught now slice through `paginateAndLink` (wrapper responses keep `total_count` at the pre-pagination total), the object-shaped endpoints follow their documented semantics (commit and compare page their `files`/`commits`, compare caps unpaginated at 250 commits/300 files and shows files only on page one, combined status and topics page their inner arrays), and the map-iteration feeds the new tests exposed (`ListAppInstallations`, `ListCheckSuitesForCommit`, license keys, follower/following sets) now sort deterministically. Verified by reversion: dropping one handler's pagination fails the gate naming the route. Per-endpoint regressions assert page slicing, `rel="next"`, and stable `total_count`

findings.finding: `milestone`, `creator`, `mentioned`, `sort`, `direction`, `since` dropped; invalid `state` silently becomes OPEN; unknown assignee returns the unfiltered list
findings.status: fixed — issue and PR rows share the documented filters, valid-but-unresolved owners select an empty set, malformed enum/date inputs 422, and stable created/updated/comment ordering is covered in both directions

findings.finding: Commit list drops six filters and hard-stops at 30 first-parent commits, so `?page=2` is always empty
findings.status: fixed — the list walks the full reachable commit graph, honors ref/path/author/since/until selectors, validates timestamps, and delegates stable page slicing and absolute Link headers to the shared paginator; the browser exposes the same selectors and page journey

findings.finding: `filter` misread as a conclusion, so GitHub's documented default `?filter=latest` returns an empty list
findings.status: fixed — the enum is validated, the default is `latest`, `all` retains reruns, and `app_id` no longer silently ignores malformed values

findings.finding: Org alert endpoints drop every filter while the repo siblings parse them
findings.status: fixed — org secret-scanning and dependabot alerts accept and apply state/secret_type/resolution (secret scanning) and state/ecosystem/package (dependabot) query parameters, with unknown values yielding zero matches rather than 400; sort/direction are honored

findings.finding: `tool_guid` dropped in three places and hardcoded `nil` in the renderer
findings.status: fixed — SARIF `tool.driver.guid` is extracted and stored on analyses and alerts; `tool.guid` is emitted from the stored value rather than hardcoded `nil`; the direct-create store paths accept a `tool_guid` parameter

findings.finding: `r.URL.Query()` never called; `includes_parents` defaults true and is dropped
findings.status: fixed — repository lists include applicable organization rulesets by default, honor `includes_parents`, `targets`, and pagination, and reject malformed query values; organization lists share the official target filter and pagination

findings.finding: `since` dropped on every comment list — the documented incremental-sync mechanism
findings.status: fixed — issue, pull-request review and commit comment lists share an inclusive RFC3339 updated-time filter; malformed timestamps consistently return 422 before pagination

findings.finding: Token-scoping endpoint decodes permissions and repositories and drops all three, returning an unnarrowed token with a 200
findings.status: fixed — scoped GitHub App user tokens persist target, permission, and repository constraints; authorization intersects all three, inspection reflects them, reload preserves them, and a scoped token cannot be widened

findings.finding: `PUT /pulls/{n}/update-branch` is a pure no-op returning 202; the body is copied to `io.Discard`
findings.status: fixed — resolves both repositories, enforces `expected_head_sha`, copies base objects for fork PRs, performs a CAS-protected three-way merge into the head, updates the recorded base SHA, and sends the resulting push through the common activity/webhook/Actions/Pages fan-out

findings.finding: `team_reviewers` decoded, counted, never used — 201 with `requested_teams: []`
findings.status: fixed — team slugs are validated in the repository owner organization, stored by immutable team ID, survive renames, render in both pull-request and requested-reviewers shapes, and can be removed through the same endpoint

findings.finding: `Location` declared and never passed; five more create fields absent entirely; unknown machine name silently no-ops
