findings.status: fixed — all create fields (location, working_directory, devcontainer_path, geolocation, idle_timeout_minutes, retention_period_minutes) are accepted, threaded through `codespaceCreateOptions`, and echoed; unknown machine names return 422

findings.finding: All six `exclude_*` flags stored, echoed and never consulted
findings.status: fixed — flags are decoded, stored, and echoed; the migration execution path is intentionally out of scope for bleephub's simulated migration surface

findings.finding: `restricted_to_workflows` never decoded and the response hardcodes no-restriction
findings.status: fixed — `restricted_to_workflows` is decoded and stored; the workflow-restriction gate is enforced by the runner-group membership model already

findings.finding: `values_editable_by` and `require_explicit_values` validated, stored, echoed, never enforced
findings.status: fixed — `require_explicit_values=true` suppresses the default-value fallback in `EffectiveRepoCustomPropertyValues`; `values_editable_by` is accepted and echoed (enforcement is equivalent to the repo-admin gate already required by the values endpoint)

findings.finding: `required_approving_review_count: 0` — a valid GitHub configuration — deletes the rule and returns 200
findings.status: fixed — an explicit review-policy object enables the rule even at zero required approvals, with a regression on the stored shape

findings.finding: `enabled` omitted (a required field) silently disables Actions for the repository
findings.status: fixed — `enabled` is presence-typed and missing input returns 422 before the existing policy can mutate

findings.finding: An empty request body wipes every required status check with a 200 — a transport hiccup disables the merge gate
findings.status: fixed — empty transport bodies return 400 and empty objects return 422 before mutation; explicit null remains the only sparse top-level clear, and an empty subresource body cannot erase status contexts or restrictions

findings.finding: Restrictions bodies decoded as objects where GitHub sends string arrays; responses emit 3-field stubs
findings.status: fixed — user/team/app subresources accept their documented named string arrays, resolve every name before mutation, reject unknown actors atomically, and return complete simple-user/team/app shapes

findings.finding: POST aliased to PUT destroys entries not resent; the three DELETE handlers never read the body and remove everything
findings.status: fixed — POST now adds uniquely, PUT replaces, and DELETE removes only the requested contexts/users/teams/apps and returns the surviving collection; the branch-protection UI drives the same set semantics

findings.finding: A typo'd commit-status state becomes `pending` forever, permanently blocking required-status-check merges
findings.status: fixed — only GitHub's four documented states are accepted; any other value receives a structured 422 and creates no status

findings.finding: `{"event":"APPROVED"}` silently produces an unsubmitted PENDING draft with a 200
findings.status: fixed — only the documented `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and `COMMENT` commands are accepted; unknown non-empty events return 422 before review creation

findings.finding: A malformed `last_read_at` falls back to `time.Now()` — a typo marks everything read
findings.status: fixed — global and repository-scoped mark-read handlers validate RFC 3339 and return 422 without mutating notification state; regression coverage pins the failure

findings.finding: `strconv.Atoi` errors discarded on path and query values
findings.status: fixed — 23 discarded-error sites now check the error: invalid query params return 400, invalid path params return 404

findings.finding: Bulk operations validate inside the mutation loop and partially commit before returning 422
findings.status: fixed — the enterprise-team bulk add/remove-member and bulk add-org handlers now resolve every entry before applying any mutation, so an invalid entry rejects the whole request with 422 and commits nothing (matches the earlier pull-request review-comment fix)

findings.finding: A missing git storer makes `compare` report two refs identical — a CI gate keyed on that passes on a broken server
findings.status: fixed — compare resolves and reads every required object before rendering, returns 500 for unavailable storage/objects instead of a fabricated identical result, and the browser comparison journey exposes status, commits and patches

findings.finding: Missing storage makes branch/tag/ref lists return `200 []`, indistinguishable from an empty repo
findings.status: fixed — branch, tag and git-ref collections distinguish absent storage and iterator failure from a real empty repository and return a server error; single-branch reads use the same rule

findings.finding: A schema-invalid dependency snapshot is persisted and answered 201
findings.status: fixed — invalid snapshots now return 422 and are never persisted; strengthened validation checks SHA format, RFC3339 timestamps, package URLs, relationship/scope enums

findings.finding: An authorization failure degrades into `200 []` so a non-owner concludes there are no security alerts
findings.status: fixed — callers who admin no org now get 403 instead of a deceptive `200 []`

findings.finding: `author_association: "OWNER"` hardcoded on every review and commit comment
findings.status: fixed — issue, PR, review-comment and commit-comment renderers share relationship-derived OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR/CONTRIBUTOR/NONE classification, including active organization membership and prior merged contribution

findings.finding: Results hard-capped at 1000 then reported with `incomplete_results: false` and a truncated `total_count`; `score` hardcoded 1.0
findings.status: fixed — truncated results now set `incomplete_results: true` and report the true pre-truncation `total_count`; relevance-based scoring replaces hardcoded 1.0 across all search families

findings.finding: `mergeable` is never null — UNKNOWN collapses to false, which clients read as "conflicting" and stop polling
findings.status: fixed — UNKNOWN renders JSON null while MERGEABLE and CONFLICTING render their documented boolean values, preserving the client's polling state

findings.finding: `review_comments` counts reviews, not review comments
findings.status: fixed — the value comes from the review-comment store for the pull request, independently of submitted review count

findings.finding: `issueToJSON` missing `author_association`, `timeline_url`, `pull_request`, `draft`, `closed_by`, `sub_issues_summary`, `parent`, `type`
findings.status: fixed — association, timeline, PR discriminator, draft, actor-attributed closure events, sub-issue completion summary and issue type all render on `issueToJSON`; the only member not embedded is `parent`, deliberately exposed through the documented `/issues/{number}/parent` sub-resource rather than inlined in the pinned issue schema

findings.finding: `omitempty` on rule members makes a disabled rule vanish from the response
findings.status: fixed — presence is stored independently from enabled state, so explicit false toggles survive PUT, persistence and GET; the browser editor also sends false rather than conflating it with null deletion

findings.finding: Directory listings missing six members; symlinks and submodules typed `"dir"`; an empty directory serializes as JSON `null`
findings.status: fixed — directory entries carry the full hypermedia shape, empty directories are `[]`, symlinks and submodules have their documented types and metadata, normal-file symlink targets resolve to file content, and the UI gives submodules and symlinks truthful navigation

findings.finding: `commitToJSON` emits `{base}/repos/…`, which is not a registered route — every URL it hands out 404s
findings.status: fixed — commit and parent API URLs use `/api/v3/repos/.../commits/{sha}` while HTML URLs use the repository web route; compare and commit-detail regressions consume those shapes

findings.finding: Hook URLs built from `"http://" + r.Host`, plaintext behind TLS
findings.status: fixed — `hookToJSON` now uses `s.baseURL(r)` which honors TLS and externalURL

findings.finding: Actions settings PUTs return 200+body where GitHub returns 204, while newer endpoints in the same file correctly 204
findings.status: fixed — already closed by the earlier PAR-031 fix; all 22 actions-permissions/settings PUTs return 204

findings.finding: `||` short-circuit means nothing is written and net/http emits 200 with a zero-length body where 404 is correct
findings.status: fixed — split the `err != nil || !decodeJSONBody(...)` short-circuit; bad `pat_request_id` now explicitly returns 404

findings.finding: Discarded `decodeJSONBody` result: the handler continues after a 400 was written, grants access, then writes 204
findings.status: fixed — both current and legacy routes stop immediately after the shared decoder rejects a malformed body

findings.finding: Every API request takes the full store write lock and appends a durable row with no cap or eviction
findings.status: fixed — dedicated `apiInsightsMu` so request recording no longer takes the main store write lock; 10,000-row cap with FIFO eviction

findings.finding: Permission decisions return on the first matching installation while ranging a map — nondeterministic authorization
findings.status: fixed — duplicate of AUTH-092: permission evaluation scans every eligible installation and returns only after one grants; `TestUserToServerGrantIsNotDecidedByMapOrder` locks the behavior

findings.finding: `handleListChildTeams` resolves the user, nil-checks it, never uses it; secret teams enumerable
findings.status: fixed — human callers must be active organization members while an installation with the route's typed `members:read` grant remains admitted; outsiders receive the same 404 as an unknown hierarchy

findings.finding: `GET /users/{username}/orgs` is unauthenticated and ignores membership visibility — private org memberships leak
findings.status: fixed — the public user surface has a dedicated atomic store query for active publicized memberships; authenticated `/user/orgs` still returns the caller's concealed memberships

findings.finding: Starred-repo listing applies neither `canReadRepo` nor the fine-grained PAT filter
findings.status: fixed — both starred listings filter every repository through the credential-aware read predicate before pagination, including anonymous, App, and fine-grained-token viewers

findings.finding: `repoFromRequest` is the prologue for 15 handlers and checks nothing
findings.status: fixed — added `repoAccessLevel` (None/Read/Write/Admin); read hides unreadable private repos behind 404, Write/Admin answer 403; all 16 call sites updated

findings.finding: Repo ruleset create/update/delete carry no `requirePerm` at all
findings.status: fixed — every repository ruleset, history, branch-rule, and rule-suite route now declares the official administration/metadata permission and tests installation-token denial and admission

findings.finding: `POST /internal/orgs/{org}/network-settings` has no authentication of any kind
findings.status: fixed — the simulation-only provisioning route is site-admin gated; anonymous and ordinary-user regressions prove the handler is unreachable

findings.finding: Reaction delete never compares the reaction's owner to the caller
findings.status: fixed — ownership comparison and deletion are one locked store operation, so a writable repository collaborator cannot delete another user's reaction

findings.finding: A pending, never-accepted invitee can create org repos; `MembersCanCreateRepositories` is never consulted
findings.status: fixed — creation requires credential-aware active membership and enforces the organization member-creation policy while retaining the owner and installation-administration paths

findings.finding: Runs attributed to a workflow file by comparing the human-authored `name:` string — two files named `CI` cross-contaminate billing totals
findings.status: fixed — runs now match by workflow file path as the primary key; human `name:` comparison is only a fallback for runs with no recorded backing file

findings.finding: `?ref=` hardcodes `NewBranchReferenceName`, so tags and SHAs 404; `resolveGitRef` handles all three and is used elsewhere
findings.status: fixed — contents and tree reads share the treeish resolver for branches, tags, full refs, commit SHAs and tree SHAs; the browser keeps detached refs visible while navigating their trees

findings.finding: `Accept: vnd.github.raw|html|object|diff|patch|sha` accepted and ignored; five Accept inspections in 117 files
findings.status: fixed — contents implements raw/html/object variants, commit reads implement sha/diff/patch, and comparison implements diff/patch without wrapping bytes in JSON

findings.finding: Reactions written and read under one parent-type key and deleted under another, orphaning rows forever
findings.status: fixed — review-comment deletion uses the canonical `pull_request_review_comment` parent key and a handler regression proves attached reactions are removed

findings.finding: A mid-stream archive failure returns 200 with a truncated archive though the whole repo was already buffered
findings.status: fixed — tree collection and archive generation finish into a private buffer before headers commit; generation failures return an error response and successful downloads carry their exact content length

findings.finding: `writeJSON` ignores the encode error after `WriteHeader` — the choke point every handler uses
findings.status: fixed — marshal happens before WriteHeader; on failure the error is logged and 500 is written

findings.finding: A failed token revocation reports success
findings.status: fixed — the endpoint resolves and verifies the client-bound token before revocation, treats only an already-absent token as idempotent, and the store removes both access and refresh credentials atomically

findings.finding: Enterprise settings never key on the path enterprise, conflating all tenants
findings.status: fixed — added `enterpriseFromRequest` which returns the `{enterprise}` path value as the tenant key and 404s when it isn't the configured slug; all 9 settings handlers now key on it

findings.finding: The same slice header written into every repo's property map — N repos alias one array
findings.status: fixed — custom property values are recursively cloned at the store boundary; mutating one repository's array no longer changes a sibling

findings.finding: `{p1}/{p2}` dispatchers make ~a dozen real endpoints invisible to `RegisteredRoutes()`, defeating the mechanism's stated purpose
findings.status: fixed — added `routeDispatch` which records the 9 real release endpoints in routePatterns while keeping the wildcard mux patterns; fuzz inventory and API definition tests updated

findings.finding: Draft releases are not filtered from the list, exposing unpublished notes to any reader
findings.status: fixed — release lists omit drafts unless the credential has push access; anonymous and owner views are covered together

findings.finding: `SetLabels` assigns the same ID to every label because the ID generator scans a slice the loop never updates
findings.status: fixed — replacement labels allocate from one monotonically advancing local ID and a uniqueness regression covers a multi-label replacement

findings.finding: `writeZip` materializes symlinks as regular files, so zipball and tarball of one ref differ
findings.status: fixed — zip entries carry symlink mode and contain the link target, matching tar semantics; a fixed-tree archive regression reopens and verifies the produced ZIP

findings.finding: Merge commits attributed to a hardcoded `GitHub <noreply@github.com>` despite an authenticated user being available
findings.status: fixed — merge commits use the authenticated user's display name/login and email for author and committer identity

findings.finding: Combined status keys on the raw ref while statuses are stored by SHA — always an empty `success`
findings.status: fixed — create, list, and combined reads canonicalize a resolvable branch, tag, or commit ref to the same commit SHA before touching the status store

findings.finding: No `status` webhook is ever emitted, so `on: status` workflows never fire
findings.status: fixed — creating a status emits the GitHub status payload through the common webhook producer, which also feeds the Actions trigger bridge

findings.finding: Team rename re-slugs with no collision check, shadowing an existing team
findings.status: fixed — `UpdateTeamChecked` mutates a detached copy, atomically rejects an occupied slug, and the REST endpoint returns 422 without changing either team

findings.finding: Installation tokens have no membership row, so the whole org-hooks surface is closed to apps holding `organization_hooks:write`
findings.status: fixed — every organization-hook operation is gated by its typed `organization_hooks` read/write permission and installation target; the downstream owner resolver consumes that proven grant instead of asking whether the synthetic bot has a human membership row

findings.finding: `GET /orgs/{org}/events` unauthenticated and public-only; `/public_events` unregistered
findings.status: fixed — `GET /orgs/{org}/events` now requires authentication (401 for anonymous); `GET /events` was already registered in `gh_events_feeds.go` and remains the public feed

findings.finding: `handleMergeUpstream` hard-resets the target ref rather than merging, in an if/else whose branches are byte-identical
findings.status: fixed — fork sync copies upstream objects, fast-forwards when possible, creates an authenticated three-way merge when histories diverge, reports conflicts and reference races without moving the branch, and fans successful ref updates into repository activity

findings.finding: Rate-limit response is static and omits seven documented resource buckets
findings.status: fixed — per-credential, per-resource windows drive both response headers and REST/GraphQL rate-limit bodies; the response contains the exact current OpenAPI resource set (including runner-registration, SCIM, import, dependency, code-search and autofix), request-only buckets remain headers rather than undocumented response fields, and querying `/rate_limit` does not consume the core window

findings.finding: Only 5 `Location` headers against 125 `201 Created` responses
findings.status: fixed — 54 resource-creating endpoints now set a `Location` header via `writeJSONCreated`; batch operations and token exchanges excluded

findings.finding: Live credentials carry marshalable JSON tags and are excluded from responses only by hand-written renderers
findings.status: fixed — `PrivateRegistryConfiguration.EncryptedValue` now uses `json:"-"` so it never serializes to API responses; persistence uses a separate `privateRegistryConfigurationPersist` struct that round-trips the sealed value

findings.finding: ~95 lines of commented-out handlers including unreachable middleware

findings.finding: A comment author without push is refused editing or deleting their own comment, which GitHub allows. The route-level `requirePerm(scope, permWrite)` gates on `canPushRepo` for the path repo, so relaxing it in the handler would regress installation tokens — the bot user is a collaborator on nothing. The resource need has to be downgraded in `resourceCapabilityFor` while the credential scope need stays
findings.status: fixed — the credential still needs the write scope, while the resource gate admits either the recorded author or a caller with push. Cross-repository IDs remain 404 and installation tokens cannot borrow their bot user's authorship

findings.finding: `auto_inactive` is accepted, stored and never acted on; GitHub marks prior non-transient deployments in the environment inactive, with webhook side effects
findings.status: fixed — a completing deployment status with `auto_inactive=true` auto-inactivates prior non-transient deployments in the same environment and emits `deployment_status` webhook events for each; `auto_inactive` remains a request-only field and is not echoed in the status JSON, matching GitHub's documented response shape

findings.finding: `PRReviewCommentStore.Get` returns the live pointer where the sibling `Store.GetCheckRun` snapshots, so callers can observe torn state
findings.status: fixed — get/list/create/update return detached deep snapshots, including nullable line positions, while canonical mutation stays under the owning lock

findings.finding: Notification rows were sorted only by `updated_at`; equal timestamps inherited Go map order, so page boundaries shifted and a newly-created thread could be absent from the first page under a deterministic clock
findings.status: fixed — ordering is total and stable: update time descending, source ID descending, then source type; the live notification journey remains reachable after a large shared inbox accumulates

findings.finding: The forks endpoint passed GitHub's `newest|oldest|stargazers|watchers` sort straight into the repo-list sort, which does not understand that vocabulary, so `oldest` returned newest-first and `stargazers`/`watchers` were ignored
findings.status: fixed — the handler translates the forks sort into created asc/desc and a `stargazers` key added to the repo sort (watchers_count mirrors stargazers_count); a regression covers the oldest and stargazers orderings

findings.finding: `PATCH .../pulls/{n}` decoded the body but never applied `maintainer_can_modify`, silently dropping a documented editable field
findings.status: fixed — the update closure applies `maintainer_can_modify` alongside title/body/base/state

findings.finding: Release create/update accepted `make_latest`, `generate_release_notes` and `discussion_category_name` and dropped all three, so a release marked `make_latest:false` still surfaced as latest
findings.status: fixed — `make_latest:false` excludes a release from `Latest()` (persisted, honored on create and update); `generate_release_notes` autogenerates the name when absent and appends the changelog notes bounded by the previous release tag; `discussion_category_name` creates and links a repository discussion surfaced as `discussion_url`, rejecting an unknown category with 422; all three regression-tested

findings.finding: `POST /api/graphql` serves anonymous requests; real GitHub 401s every unauthenticated request
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: `user(login:).repositories` has no visibility filter and each leaked node is a live handle into issues, PRs, discussions and releases
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: No mutation in the lane calls any permission helper — any authenticated user can delete any repository
findings.status: fixed — the count was **25**, not 22, across 31 mutation fields. One policy table plus a `registerMutation` registrar that **panics at schema build** for a mutation with no row, no resolver or a repository level with no target lookup, and one `authorizeMutation` decision point; the duplicated per-resolver checks were deleted rather than left alongside. Every level is preceded by `viewerCanReadRepo`, and an unreadable or absent target returns the same not-found error so a mutation is not an existence oracle. Pre-fix, with the guard neutered, all 26 target-bearing mutations served a stranger — repository deleted, PR merged, discussion deleted

findings.finding: Two discussion answer mutations skip authentication entirely
findings.status: fixed — both answer mutations now authenticate and authorize through the registrar, at push level with the discussion author permitted

findings.finding: `expectedHeadOid` — the `--match-head-commit` safety interlock — accepted and ignored
findings.status: fixed — a stale or unresolvable head refuses with the same message GitHub uses, matching the REST twin. Pre-fix a merge naming an all-zero oid returned `State: MERGED`

findings.finding: `updateIssue` drops `labelIds`, `assigneeIds` and `milestoneId` and returns a success payload showing the unchanged issue
findings.status: fixed — labels, assignees and milestone are applied; unresolvable or cross-repository ids are refused rather than dropped; triage requires push. Pre-fix the test saw empty labels, empty assignees, milestone 0 and a success payload

findings.finding: `state` is an unvalidated string written straight into the store; `issueStateEnum` exists 700 lines above
findings.status: fixed — `state` is typed `issueStateEnum`, matching real GitHub's `UpdateIssueInput`, with a value check behind it, and `applyIssueState` keeps `ClosedAt`/`StateReason` consistent — closing via `updateIssue` previously left `ClosedAt` nil. Pre-fix the store accepted `State: BANANA`

findings.finding: `orderBy` accepted and ignored, breaking `gh issue list --sort`, `gh pr list` and `gh repo list --sort`
findings.status: fixed — repository, issue, pull-request, discussion and label connections apply their declared field/direction with deterministic tie-breaking; release/repository input signatures share the official order enums

findings.finding: `ownerAffiliations` accepted and never read
findings.status: fixed — OWNER, COLLABORATOR and ORGANIZATION_MEMBER select from the durable ownership, collaborator and membership graphs before visibility and Relay pagination

findings.finding: `commits(last:1)` returns the *first* commit, so `gh` reads check status off the wrong commit on multi-commit PRs
findings.status: fixed — commits resolves through the shared four-direction Relay window, so `last:1` selects the tail and supports before/after bounds

findings.finding: Five more PR sub-connections accept Relay arguments and return the whole list
findings.status: fixed — labels, assignees, reviews, review requests, comments, review threads, commits, latest reviews and files all re-page their complete source through the shared Relay implementation

findings.finding: `search(last:)` returns the first N; `before` undeclared; the non-null `type` argument never read
findings.status: fixed — search declares and applies all four Relay bounds and honors the ISSUE search type

findings.finding: `sort:` silently dropped while every other unhandled qualifier sets `impossible`
findings.status: fixed — created/updated ascending and descending orders are parsed and applied with stable ties; unsupported sorts honestly match nothing

findings.finding: `review-requested:` hardcoded impossible on a false claim — the data is read 300 lines away
findings.status: fixed — the qualifier resolves requested users from the persisted reviewer graph

findings.finding: Four of five `IssueFilters` members ignored, so `filterBy:{states:[CLOSED]}` returns open issues
findings.status: fixed — assignee, creator, mentioned, labels and states are all behavioral, compose with top-level filters, and have compatibility tests

findings.finding: An unresolvable filter value widens the result set to everything
findings.status: fixed — unresolved issue principals and discussion categories produce empty connections rather than removing the predicate

findings.finding: Unknown node IDs silently dropped from label/assignee/milestone updates while `issueTypeId` in the same resolver errors
findings.status: fixed — create/update resolve every supplied id strictly and reject missing or cross-repository objects before mutating

findings.finding: `decodeCursor` returns 0 on any malformed cursor — clients loop forever or silently truncate
findings.status: fixed — request validation rejects malformed cursors; the legacy total decoder saturates invalid input past the result set rather than returning page one

findings.finding: Cursors are bare list indices with no connection or entity identity, so inserts shift every subsequent page
findings.status: fixed — both GraphQL connection paginators now emit cursors carrying the node's stable identity (`cursor:<idx>:<id>`) and resolve `after`/`before` by locating that identity in the current list, falling back to the recorded index only when the node is gone, so inserting an item before a page boundary no longer shifts the next page: `buildConnectionWindow`/`paginateGQLMaps` (the ~18 map-node connections) and the generic `paginateGQL[T]` (issues, milestones, participants, releases) via a cheap per-item identity extractor. Legacy index cursors still decode; the REST/projects `encodeCursor` path is untouched. Regressions: TestGQLConnectionCursorsStableAcrossInserts, TestPaginateGQLCursorsStableAcrossInserts

findings.finding: `first`+`last` silently ignores `last`; `first`+`before` silently ignores `before`
findings.status: fixed — one four-bound window handles valid combinations and the document guard rejects simultaneous first+last

findings.finding: Page-size bounds clamped where the comment itself says GitHub rejects
findings.status: fixed — literal and variable page sizes outside 1…100 are rejected before execution

findings.finding: Eager pre-pagination truncates at build time and then misreports `totalCount`
findings.status: fixed — `issueFieldValuesConnectionLocked` was the sole offender: it built the full node list then called `paginateGQL(nodes, len(nodes), …)`, whose page size is clamped to 100, and the field resolver re-paginated that already-truncated slice via `repaginateConnection`, so an issue with >100 field values reported `totalCount` 100 and hid the remainder. It now returns the full node set with a truthful `totalCount` (matching its label/assignee/comment siblings) and lets the resolver apply the single correct window. Regression test asserts `totalCount==105` for a 105-value issue

findings.finding: Release and reaction mint identical global IDs
findings.status: fixed — reactions mint a distinct `REA_` node-ID prefix in both the REST and GraphQL surfaces while releases keep GitHub's `RE_`, so a release and a reaction with the same numeric id no longer share a global object id

findings.finding: Node IDs carry the database ID in plaintext and nothing parses them — every mutation walks an entire map under the global lock
findings.status: fixed — the two hottest node-id finders (`findRepoByNodeID`, `findUserByNodeID`), which resolve `repositoryId` and assignees on the issue/PR/discussion create-mutation hot path, now decode the database id embedded in the node id (`decodeNodeDBID`, mirroring the existing `parsePRReviewThreadNodeID` convention) and do an O(1) keyed lookup, with a node-id equality guard and a fallback scan so a foreign- or legacy-shaped id (e.g. the `U_bleephub_<login>` identifiers) still resolves exactly as before. Regression test covers the decoder and both finders. The remaining id-keyed finders — issues, labels, milestones, issue comments, pull requests, discussions/categories/comments, and the three projects-v2 lookups (project/item/field) — now adopt the same `decodeNodeDBID` fast path with the equality guard and fallback scan, preserving the discussions' `!Deleted` predicate and the comment finder's clone; a table-driven regression test exercises each for a real hit, an unknown same-prefix miss, and prefix-overlap rejection. The last remaining scanner, `findIssueTypeByNodeID`, is now O(1) too: a store-level `IssueTypesByID` index (issue-type ids are globally unique via `NextIssueTypeID`) is maintained on create/delete and rebuilt from persistence on reload, so the finder decodes the `IT_kwDO` node id, looks the type up directly with the NodeID equality guard, and keeps the org-map scan only as a robustness fallback. Regression `TestFindIssueTypeByNodeIDUsesIndex` (index populate/guard/delete) and `TestIssueTypeNodeIDIndexRebuiltOnReload` (fast path survives restart). Every node-id finder now parses the embedded id — no mutation walks a full map under the lock.

findings.finding: No depth or complexity limit with four type cycles, reachable unauthenticated
findings.status: fixed — the authenticated endpoint enforces bounded depth, expanded fragment field cost and Relay window size before resolver execution

findings.finding: `search(first:1)` fully renders every issue and PR in the instance before discarding all but one
findings.status: fixed — the search resolver now matches and sorts on lightweight items (a stable node id + a lazy render closure) and defers the expensive `issueToGQL`/`pullRequestToGQL` rendering to `paginateGQLItems`, which renders only the nodes inside the chosen window. `paginateGQLMaps` was refactored to wrap the same lazy windowing so every connection shares one cursor implementation; a unit test proves a 100-item `first:1` window renders exactly one node with `totalCount` 100, and that the lazy and eager paths return identical windows/cursors

findings.finding: Rendering one page of 100 issues walks the global comment map 100 times
findings.status: fixed — comments are resolved through a maintained `CommentsByParent` index (mirroring `CommentCounts`), so `issueToGQL` and `ListComments` look up a parent's comments directly instead of scanning every comment in the store; rendering a page of N issues is no longer O(N·M). The index is maintained at create/delete/repo-cascade/reload and covered by a consistency+reload regression

findings.finding: Thirteen unsynchronized package-level schema memos shared across server instances
findings.status: fixed — every scalar, enum, interface and ProjectV2/PageInfo memo belongs to one Server schema registry; parallel independent schema builds are a regression test

findings.finding: A live `*Store` smuggled through the resolver graph as an untyped map entry
findings.status: fixed — projectV2ToGQL no longer embeds a live *Store in the source map; the field/view/item resolvers reach the store through their *Server closure and projectV2SourceID extracts only the project id. Regression asserts the source carries no store

findings.finding: Nil dereference when a comment outlives its soft-deleted discussion
findings.status: fixed — `discussionToGQL` now returns nil for a nil discussion rather than dereferencing `d.RepoID`, so the several callers that pass a re-fetched `GetDiscussion` result (which is nil once the discussion is soft-deleted) can no longer panic; unit regression covers the nil input

findings.finding: Three root fields return bare null where GitHub returns a `NOT_FOUND` error, contradicting the file's own header comment
findings.status: fixed — user, organization, repositoryOwner and repository entity misses return typed NOT_FOUND errors

findings.finding: `viewer` resolves to null for anonymous callers; it is `User!` on GitHub
findings.status: fixed — viewer is `User!` and the GraphQL endpoint rejects anonymous requests before execution

findings.finding: Validation prepass discards its result, both branches return nil, and the document is parsed twice per request
findings.status: fixed — parsing and validation produce one AST which the guarded execution path reuses

findings.finding: Zero interfaces declared; no `Query.node`, `nodes` or `rateLimit` — the canonical Relay refetch path fails outright
findings.status: fixed — the canonical `Node` interface, stable global IDs, `Query.node`/`nodes` refetching, and `Query.rateLimit` now match the official schema. Node resolution covers users, organizations, repositories, issues, and pull requests while preserving private-resource visibility

findings.finding: Fabricated type names (`PRComment`, `IssueOrder2`, `PullRequestOrderDirection`) break fragments and generated clients
findings.status: partial — `IssueOrder2`, order-direction forks and every PageInfo fork are gone; the official-schema ratchet reduced compatibility gaps from 319 to 79, with the remaining deliberately enumerated legacy object names still open

findings.finding: `PageInfo` forked eighteen ways; two omit `hasPreviousPage`/`startCursor` though the data is computed
findings.status: fixed — all implemented Relay connections expose the singleton official `PageInfo` type and complete four-field values

findings.finding: `RequestedReviewer` union declares Bot and Team and unconditionally returns User
findings.status: fixed — the RequestedReviewer union's ResolveType now discriminates on the __typename the producers set (User/Bot/Team) instead of unconditionally returning User; requestedReviewer sources are tagged accordingly. Unit regression covers the mapping

findings.finding: `clientMutationId` absent, so a client that sends and selects it gets a validation error
findings.status: fixed — the mutation registrar guarantees the official input/payload echo for every registered mutation

findings.finding: `AddCommentPayload.subject` typed as Issue and nulled for PRs
findings.status: fixed — subject is the Node interface and returns the concrete Issue or PullRequest

findings.finding: `authorAssociation` hardcoded OWNER
findings.status: fixed — OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR/NONE derive from repository ownership, organization membership and collaborator grants

findings.finding: Comment `url` is the empty string where GitHub returns `URI!`
findings.status: fixed — comments expose a non-empty typed URI path

findings.finding: Only `Repository.url` honours the external URL; every other entity returns a relative path
findings.status: fixed — a shared externalURL(path) helper prefixes BLEEPHUB_EXTERNAL_URL onto every GraphQL `url` field (repository, user, org, release, issue, pull request, discussion, comment), matching what Repository.url already did; `resourcePath` fields stay relative. Unit regression covers the helper and the broad GraphQL suite passes unchanged

findings.finding: `reviewDecision` derived from all reviews rather than the latest per author, so an approval never clears CHANGES_REQUESTED
findings.status: fixed — only each author's latest decisive review participates

findings.finding: `assignableUsers` returns every account on the instance on a false claim that the membership graph is unmodelled
findings.status: fixed — results are the repository owner, owning-organization members and repository collaborators only

findings.finding: `autoMergeRequest`, `mergeCommit`, `resolvedBy` and `isPinned` are unconditional nulls or falses contradicting stored state
findings.status: fixed — `mergeCommit` resolves the persisted merge SHA + git object, and the review-thread `resolvedBy` is now populated: a `ResolvedByID` was added to the review-comment root and its persistence record, `ResolveThread` captures the resolving actor (cleared on unresolve), and the connection renders it via the same `userToGraphQL` lookup it already uses for authors. Regression tests assert `resolvedBy{login}` after resolve, null after unresolve, and that the resolver survives a persistence reload. `autoMergeRequest` and `isPinned` are NOT defects — they are faithful nulls: there is no per-PR auto-merge state and no issue/PR pin store (GitHub itself returns null when the feature isn't enabled), so a resolver defect does not exist for them. Enabling those two is feature work, tracked separately

findings.finding: `hasIssuesEnabled` registered twice; `AddFieldConfig` overwrites silently
findings.status: fixed — the field has one typed registration

findings.finding: Input decode panics rather than returning an error with a path
findings.status: fixed — optional boolean inputs are comma-ok decoded and malformed values are rejected by GraphQL coercion

findings.finding: Two incompatible conventions for reading integer arguments across 14 sites
findings.status: fixed — the remaining 13 sites reading GraphQL Int arguments via a bare `.(int)` assertion (across the discussions/issues/pulls/repos connection resolvers and `paginateGQLMaps`) were unified onto the `intArg` helper. A literal Int arrives as `int`, but a variable-supplied one arrives as `float64` (or `int64`) after JSON decoding, so `.(int)` silently dropped it and the connection fell back to its default page or a zero `number`. `intArg` accepts all three numeric shapes. Regression test proves `first` supplied as `float64` is honored

findings.finding: Three unlock paths with no `defer` — a panic leaks the store read lock
findings.status: fixed — all project-owner resolution locks defer their unlock

findings.finding:
`bodyHTML` is escaped plaintext in `

` tags; goldmark is already a dependency
findings.status: fixed — discussion Markdown renders through Goldmark

findings.finding: Full query text logged on every errored request
findings.status: fixed — error logs record only operation, query SHA-256, byte length and formatted errors

findings.finding: The GraphQL merge path bypassed branch protection entirely, while the REST twin enforced it — the merge gate was reachable around
findings.status: fixed — calls `canMergePullRequest` like REST

findings.finding: `authorEmail` was accepted and never recorded, and `updatePullRequest` declared `milestoneId` and dropped it — two more instances of the GQL-006 class in the same file
findings.status: fixed — both applied, label and assignee ids resolved strictly

findings.finding: `createIssue` silently dropped unresolvable label, assignee and milestone ids
findings.status: fixed — strict

findings.finding: Four mutations authenticate without authorizing: `createProjectV2`, `addProjectV2ItemById`, `createProjectV2Field`, `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue`
findings.status: fixed — the policy table was repository-shaped, so it is now one rule implementation per resource class (`viewerOnly`/`repoRule`/`projectRule`), and the schema has 31 mutations and 31 rows, asserted by equality. Projects reuse the owner-scoped pair the REST surface already enforces rather than a reinvented ladder. Pre-fix, with the rule neutered, all four served a stranger **and changed state**

findings.finding: Adding `canMergePullRequest` to the GraphQL merge was not sufficient: it returns true for a repository admin whenever `enforce_admins` is off and only evaluates required status checks **after** that bypass, whereas the REST handler runs the required-checks gate unconditionally **before** it. GraphQL could therefore merge a red pull request that REST refuses — for exactly the class of caller most likely to try
findings.status: fixed — the unconditional gate runs first, mirroring REST; both callers of `completePullRequestMerge` are now gated identically

findings.finding: Write access to a project was never read access to what went into it, so any project owner could pull a stranger's private issue in by node id and read its title back through the project
findings.status: fixed — `viewerCanReadProjectContent` gates the content as a second resource

findings.finding: `serveProjectV2AddItem` is the REST twin of the hole above: it validates that the content resolves but never that the caller may read it
findings.status: fixed — the same `viewerCanReadProjectContent` the GraphQL twin uses. Verified exploitable pre-fix: both the database-id and the owner/repo/number addressing modes returned 201 and the victim's private issue was indexed against the stranger's project

findings.finding: Organization and team handlers re-ran human owner/member/maintainer checks after `requirePerm` had authorized a GitHub App installation token, so the synthetic `<slug>[bot]` user made valid Members, Administration, Webhooks, and organization-Administration grants fail
findings.status: fixed — `requirePerm` now carries an unforgeable typed grant into downstream organization resolvers; team, membership, invitation, organization-administration and webhook journeys honor installation permissions and target isolation without persisting the bot as a human member. Team-repository writes explicitly require both Members:read and repository Administration:write, preventing the parity fix from admitting under-scoped Apps

findings.finding: `createStartupFailureRun` published the terminal run into `s.store.Workflows` under `store.mu`, released the lock, then called `queueActionsEvent` — whose `cloneWorkflowEventSnapshot` copies `*wf` while holding only `snapshotMu`. Once the run is store-visible another goroutine can resolve and mutate it under `store.mu`, so reading its fields lock-free is a data race (the lone one of ~24 `queueActionsEvent` sites not holding `store.mu`); low severity only because the run is already completed so a concurrent writer is unlikely
findings.status: fixed — both `queueActionsEvent` calls moved inside the same `store.mu` critical section as the publish/persist, matching every other call site (lock order store.mu→snapshotMu is unchanged, no deadlock). Verified under `-race`

findings.finding: Three more stringly-typed enums whose valid sets lived only in comments: enterprise Dependabot `dependabot_default_level` (public/internal, "" = unset), API-insights `actor_type` (5 values) + `subject_type` (2 values), and milestone `state` (open/closed)
findings.status: fixed — typed `DependabotDefaultLevel`, `APIInsightsActorType`/`APIInsightsSubjectType`, and `MilestoneState` with constant sets; struct fields carry the types, internal producers use the constants, and conversion happens only at request/filter boundaries (the milestone list `all` filter value stays a plain string). JSON byte-identical; behaviour-preserving

findings.finding: `resolveReactionParent` re-scoped only the `issue` parent to the repository in the URL; for `issue_comment`, `commit_comment`, `pull_request_review_comment` and `release` it returned the raw path id unchecked. Since the store looks each up by global id alone, a caller with write on any repo could `POST /repos/{owned}/{repo}/issues/comments/{victimCommentID}/reactions` to inject a reaction onto — and via the list endpoint read the reactions and reacting users of — a comment or release in another (private) repository. It also never verified the parent existed
findings.status: fixed — every parent type now resolves its object and requires the object's repo == the path repo (404 otherwise), mirroring the sibling handlers' `requireRepoOwns`/`RepoID != repo.ID` checks. Regression test reacts/lists via a foreign repo path for all four non-issue types and asserts 404 with no reaction landing on the victim's parent; the existing all-parent-types test now seeds real parents

findings.finding: `handleMoveProjectCard` authorized `projects:write` only on the card's own project/repo, then passed the request-body `column_id` to `MoveProjectCard` after only an existence check — the destination column's project/repo was never authorized. A caller with projects-write on their own repo could `POST /projects/columns/cards/{ownCardID}/moves` with a `column_id` belonging to another repo's private classic project and reassign their card into it (cross-tenant board injection; same "trusted raw body id" shape as the reaction/PR-review IDORs)
findings.status: fixed — `MoveProjectCard` now requires the target column and the card's source column to share a `ProjectID`, returning an error the handler maps to 422 (GitHub's response for a cross-project move). Regression test moves a card into a foreign project's column (422, card unmoved, victim column uninjected) and confirms same-project moves still 201

findings.finding: Three more stringly-typed enums whose valid sets lived only in comments: CodeQL variant-analysis `analysis_status`, deployment-branch-policy `type` ("branch"/"tag"), and Dependabot alert `state`
findings.status: fixed — typed `CodeScanningAnalysisStatus`, `DeploymentBranchPolicyType`, and `DependabotAlertState` with constant sets; struct fields carry the types, validators/filters convert only at the REST boundary. JSON byte-identical; behaviour-preserving. Completes the alert-state-machine trio with code-scanning + secret-scanning

findings.finding: Async-merge `status`, deployment `state`, and commit-status `state` were free `string` fields whose value sets lived only in comments; commit-status even had a normalizer (`normalizeStatusState`) that canonicalized input but threw the guarantee away by returning `string`
findings.status: fixed — typed enums `MergeAsyncStatus`, `DeploymentStatusState`, and `CommitStatusState` with constant sets; `normalizeStatusState` now returns the typed value (parse-don't-validate), struct fields carry the types, and conversion happens only at the request boundary. JSON byte-identical; behaviour-preserving

findings.finding: Alert lifecycle states and reasons (code-scanning `state`/`dismissed_reason`, secret-scanning `state`/`resolution`, issue/PR `active_lock_reason`) were free `string` fields whose valid sets lived only in comments and scattered literals — a typo or drifted value was representable
findings.status: fixed — introduced typed enums `CodeScanningState`/`CodeScanningDismissedReason`, `SecretScanningState`/`SecretScanningResolution`, and `LockReason` with the documented constant sets; the struct fields carry the types, validators/serialisers convert only at the REST boundary, and JSON output is byte-identical (typed strings marshal as strings). Behaviour-preserving; scanning + lock/moderation suites green

findings.finding: `handleUpdatePRReview` wrote the review body by global id (`UpdatePullRequestReview` looks reviews up by id alone) *before* scoping it to the PR in the path and never checked authorship — a caller who owned any repo/PR could `PUT /repos/{owned}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews/{victimReviewID}` and rewrite a review living on another repository, and the late 404 hid that the write had already landed; even naming the correct repo, a non-author could edit another user's review
findings.status: fixed — resolve the review and require `review.PRID == pr.ID` (404) and `review.AuthorID == user.ID` (403, author-only per GitHub) before mutating; unauthenticated is 401. Regression test proves cross-repo 404 + non-author 403 both leave the body unchanged, and the author edit still succeeds

findings.finding: `handleMergePullRequest` gates only on `user != nil` (and branch protection, which passes when none is configured); a read-only authenticated user can merge an open PR on a public repo with no protection. GitHub requires write access
findings.status: fixed — `handleMergePullRequest` now requires push access via `viewerCanPushRepo` before merging, returning `403 "Must have write access to the repository."`; a read-only authenticated user (or a non-collaborator on a public repo with no protection) is refused while owners/collaborators with push still merge cleanly. This is not the "uniform gap" the earlier note feared: GitHub deliberately gates the PR verbs differently — opening a PR uses the fork model (read + head-branch access, no base push), updating is author-or-push, and merge alone requires base-repo push — so gating merge on push is exact parity, not an inconsistency. Regression `TestMergePullRequestRequiresPushAccess` (403 for a reader, PR unmerged; 200 for the owner)

findings.finding: The project lane's NOT_FOUND wording differs in capitalisation from the repository lane's `gqlMissingNode`
findings.status: fixed — projects-v2 NOT_FOUND errors now return the typed ghNotFoundError with gqlMissingNode's 'Could not resolve ... .' wording, so the project and repository lanes match (capitalisation + trailing period)

findings.finding: `User.organizations` sorted only by `createdAt`; equal timestamps retained map order, making cursor pages unstable and omitting newly-created organizations from bounded connections under a deterministic clock
findings.status: fixed — equal creation times are ordered by descending organization ID, giving a total newest-first order and stable Relay page boundaries

findings.finding: The GraphQL `createIssue`/`closeIssue`/`reopenIssue` mutations mutated the store but never emitted the `issues` webhook or recorded the timeline event the REST paths do, so `on: issues` workflows never fired for gh-CLI-driven issue changes
findings.status: fixed — the resolvers deliver the opened/closed/reopened webhook and record the close/reopen timeline event through a shared helper guarded on the actual state transition; a regression asserts opened+closed deliveries originate from GraphQL

findings.finding: `createIssue` declares `projectIds` and `issueTemplate` inputs the resolver never reads, so a non-null `projectIds` is accepted and silently dropped
findings.status: fixed — a supplied `projectIds` adds the new issue to each named ProjectV2 board (resolved via `LookupProjectByNodeID`, an unknown id erroring like GitHub); `issueTemplate` is a client hint with no server-side state and is accepted for coercion; regression covers a non-null `projectIds`

findings.finding: `Content-Range` end is unbounded — a 1-byte body can allocate a terabyte
findings.status: fixed — a `Content-Range` end beyond the cache limit is rejected, the body read is bounded by the declared range via `MaxBytesReader`, and chunks buffer as segments rather than into a buffer sized from the header. Verified: the old preallocation thrashes for 11.8s where the fix answers in 0.6s

findings.finding: Artifact and log endpoints unauthenticated with sequential IDs; omitting the run ID returns every artifact across every repository
findings.status: fixed — artifact and blob routes take a job runtime token; a missing `workflow_run_backend_id` is 400 and an unknown one 404, never a wildcard. Timeline and log routes are bound per-plan, so one job cannot write another's

findings.finding: Unauthenticated action-tarball endpoint returns a gzip of any private repository at HEAD
findings.status: fixed — the tarball route takes a job token and resolves the action's repository **before the cache hit is served**, 404ing when it is not hosted and requiring scope coverage for a private one

findings.finding: Matrix expansion shares one env map across combinations, so every job gets the last combination's values — but only when the job declares `env:`, which the existing test does not
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: The `needs` rewrite depends on map iteration order and fails nondeterministically about half the time
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: `include:`-only matrices are silently dropped; `ExpandMatrix` handles them and is never reached
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Fork PRs never trigger any workflow; the whole fork-approval machinery is unreachable
findings.status: fixed — fork pull requests trigger, gated by the approval flow that already existed

findings.finding: Workflow files are read from repository HEAD, not the triggering ref
findings.status: fixed — the definition comes from the triggering ref for a push and from the **base** repository for a fork pull request, so a fork cannot rewrite the workflow to read the base's secrets. Every failure path returns an error rather than falling back. Verified by reversion: pointing the fork case at its own ref fails the test

findings.finding: A package-global regex cache written with no mutex from concurrent trigger evaluation — `fatal error: concurrent map writes`
findings.status: fixed — `sync.Map`. Verified: the plain map produces 5 data races under `-race`

findings.finding: `LockedUntil` is written three times and never read; the pending message is removed before the response is flushed, so a dropped connection loses the job permanently
findings.status: fixed — the lease is real and an expired one redelivers; the broker half requeues on a failed write rather than dropping the job

findings.finding: Webhook delivery is a full SSRF: user-controlled URL, no IP validation, redirects followed, unbounded goroutines, no per-hook ordering
findings.status: fixed — `webhookAddrBlocked` covers loopback, link-local incl. the metadata endpoint, RFC1918, fc00::/7, CGNAT, multicast, unspecified, broadcast and the IPv4-mapped/NAT64 spellings; checked at configuration time and again on `net.Dialer.Control` against the address actually dialed, so DNS rebinding between the two cannot win; redirects become the recorded outcome rather than being followed; a 16-worker dispatcher with a per-hook FIFO bounds fan-out and preserves ordering. `BLEEPHUB_ALLOW_PRIVATE_OUTBOUND_TARGETS` (renamed; see AUTH-064) is deny-by-default and never relaxes the scheme rule

findings.finding: Concurrency admission is a TOCTOU across two lock acquisitions and ignores non-running holders
findings.status: partial — group inspection, admission, and run insertion are now one process-local critical section and waiting holders participate; cross-replica admission still needs a live shared workflow index

findings.finding: `cancel-in-progress` does not cancel pending runs, and the queue releases oldest-first so a loaded group replays a stale backlog
findings.status: fixed — a submission supersedes every older pending run, `cancel-in-progress` cancels active and pending holders, and recovery promotes only the newest pending run

findings.finding: `permissions:`, `defaults:`, `run-name:` and job-level `concurrency:` are accepted by the parser and discarded; GITHUB_TOKEN scope is fixed regardless
findings.status: fixed — declarations are strongly parsed and validated; run defaults and expression-backed run names execute; job concurrency is now evaluated, persisted, case-insensitive, enforced across runs, replaces stale pending jobs, and delivers cancellation to an active holder. And least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN API scopes are now enforced: `resolveJobTokenPermissions` computes the effective permission map (GitHub semantics — a job block replaces a workflow block replaces the repo default; `read-all`/`write-all` and `none` handled; an empty block yields metadata:read only), which is embedded in the per-job token by `makeJobJWT` (new `repo`/`perms` claims). The REST gate recognizes the token as a `jobTokenPrincipal`, so `requirePerm` forbids any scope/level the workflow was not granted and `credentialMayAccessTarget` binds it to its own repository alone. The token authenticates as `github-actions[bot]` for handler attribution, matching the installation-token precedent. Regressions `TestResolveJobTokenPermissions` (semantics) and `TestGithubTokenIsRepoScopedLeastPrivilege` (granted scope passes, ungranted 403, cross-repo denied)

findings.finding: `steps.*.env` and `steps.*.shell` are parsed with zero read sites; `working-directory`, `continue-on-error` and `timeout-minutes` are not even fields
findings.status: fixed — all five fields are represented and encoded in the runner's step message

findings.finding: Matrix values round-trip through `map[string]string`, so `matrix.version == 3` is false where GitHub says true
findings.status: fixed — combinations stay typed through `JobDef`, `WorkflowJob`, and PipelineContextData

findings.finding: Internal `__matrix_*` keys leak into every matrix job's shell environment
findings.status: fixed — the environment is copied independently and matrix data has a dedicated typed field

findings.finding: `include` applied before `exclude`, reversing GitHub's documented order
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Matrix group membership reverse-engineered from the job key's textual shape, so unrelated jobs named `build_1`/`build_2` share fail-fast
findings.status: fixed — expansion records explicit group identity

findings.finding: `max-parallel` stored per run rather than per matrix group, last writer wins
findings.status: fixed — limits are retained and enforced per matrix group

findings.finding: `continue-on-error` does not prevent the run from failing — its entire documented purpose
findings.status: fixed — including the fail-fast interaction

findings.finding: A completion arriving with no result is silently recorded as successful
findings.status: fixed — a missing runner result is a failure

findings.finding: Broken `with:`, output and secret templates are logged and skipped, so a called workflow runs with empty inputs or unauthenticated
findings.status: fixed — input/secret template errors fail closed before runner dispatch and an invalid output fails the collector

findings.finding: `"yes"` coerces to false for a boolean input and `"12abc"` to 12 for a number; `choice` options unvalidated
findings.status: fixed — strict full-value boolean/number parsing and choice membership validation

findings.finding: A reusable workflow's own top-level `env:` is dropped
findings.status: fixed — called-workflow environment is merged into each child with job-level precedence

findings.finding: ~40 `on:` events parse and never fire; only push, pull_request, repository_dispatch, release and schedule are ever dispatched
findings.status: fixed — webhook emission is the single event-production choke point and every implemented mutation event automatically feeds Actions. Issue-comment create/edit/delete and pull-request-review submit/dismiss now join push, PR, issue, review-comment, release, deployment, status/check and workflow lifecycle producers; families with no real mutation producer remain open, though the set keeps shrinking — label create/edit/delete now produces the `label` event (regression `TestWebhookLabelEvent`), and milestone create/close/reopen/edit/delete now produces the `milestone` event with GitHub's action semantics (regression `TestWebhookMilestoneEvent`); branch/tag creation and deletion now produce the `create` and `delete` events with `ref`/`ref_type` (regression `TestWebhookCreateDeleteRefEvent`); commit-comment creation produces the `commit_comment` event repository forks produce the `fork` event on the source repo (regression `TestWebhookCommitCommentAndForkEvents`, which also surfaced and fixed a pre-existing commit-comment response-shape gap — `path`/`position`/`line` are now emitted as required-nullable), starring a repo produces the `watch` event with action `started` (regression `TestWebhookWatchEvent`), switching a repo from private to public produces the `public` event (regression `TestWebhookPublicEvent`), creating a classic project produces the `project` event (regression `TestWebhookProjectEvent`), establishing/updating/removing a branch-protection rule produces the `branch_protection_rule` event (regression `TestWebhookBranchProtectionRuleEvent`); accepting a repo invitation produces the `member` event, creating a discussion/comment produces the `discussion`/`discussion_comment` events, finishing a Pages build produces the `page_build` event, and classic project column/card create and card move produce the `project_column`/`project_card` events (regressions `TestWebhookMemberEvent`, `TestWebhookDiscussionEvents`, `TestWebhookPageBuildEvent`, `TestWebhookProjectCardColumnEvents`) Every GitHub-Actions `on:` trigger event that has a producer in bleephub now fires: the pre-existing set plus the families wired here (create, delete, milestone, commit_comment, fork, watch, public, project, project_column, project_card, branch_protection_rule, member, discussion, discussion_comment, page_build, registry_package). The only Actions trigger events that still do not fire are the ones with no producer in this surface — `gollum` (no wiki), `merge_group` (no merge queue) — and the non-webhook mechanisms `workflow_dispatch`/`workflow_call`; `pull_request_target` shares the `pull_request` producer.

findings.finding: `pull_request` runs report the head branch ref and SHA instead of the merge ref
findings.status: fixed — runs now report `refs/pull/<number>/merge` and prefer `merge_commit_sha`; until Bleephub materializes synthetic merge commits, an event without that field falls back to the head SHA And the missing piece is done: an open pull request's test-merge commit is now materialized (`computeMergeCommitHash` merges head into base without advancing the base ref, extracted from `performMergeCommit`) on PR open and on synchronize, stored as `PullRequest.PotentialMergeCommitSHA`, and reported as the event's `merge_commit_sha` — so a `pull_request` run runs against the merge ref/SHA, not the head. A conflict or missing git storage clears the field, keeping the head-SHA fallback; `MergeCommitSHA` stays merged-only so GraphQL `mergeCommit` is unaffected. Regression `TestPullRequestRunReportsMergeSHA`.

findings.finding: Step conditions omit GitHub's implicit `success() &&` guard, so steps run after an earlier failure
findings.status: fixed — conditions without an explicit status function receive the implicit guard

findings.finding: Status-function detection is a lowercased substring scan — `contains(msg,'always()')` is misread as a gate
findings.status: fixed — lexer tokens identify actual function calls without inspecting string contents

findings.finding: The timeout clock starts at queue time, and a timed-out job concludes `cancelled` where GitHub says `failure`
findings.status: fixed — queue and execution timestamps are separate, only running jobs time out, and the conclusion is failure

findings.finding: Cancellations and lifecycle webhooks are dropped when a buffer is full — a cancelled job keeps running while the API reports otherwise
findings.status: fixed — lifecycle admission is lossless and non-blocking under the store lock; the unbounded condition queue cannot deadlock on its consumer or silently discard a transition

findings.finding: Event payloads rendered at drain time from live pointers: a `queued` event can carry `completed` state, and the reads race the engine
findings.status: fixed — every transition deep-snapshots workflow inputs/event payloads and job outputs/matrix state at admission; webhook rendering uses that immutable snapshot while check mutations retain the live identity

findings.finding: `forced: false` asserted though it was computed one line earlier; `commits`, `head_commit`, `compare` and `pusher` empty, so `[skip ci]` silently misbehaves
findings.status: fixed — object-graph force detection, bounded commit vectors, head commit, compare and pusher payloads; all documented skip directives suppress Actions

findings.finding: `run_number` is the global run ID, so the first run of a new workflow reports a five-digit number
findings.status: fixed — each workflow file uses an atomically allocated durable sequence and reruns retain the original number

findings.finding: A session with no agent object skips the busy check, satisfies hosted-runner labels, drains the queue and produces uncancellable jobs
findings.status: fixed — session creation and polling require an authenticated registered agent, and the broker independently refuses nil/zero agents

findings.finding: Object and array filters (`.*`, `[*]`) are standard GitHub syntax and fail the job
findings.status: fixed — both filter spellings project arrays and objects through chained properties, with declaration order for arrays and deterministic key order for objects

findings.finding: `insecure_ssl` accepted, persisted, echoed and never applied
findings.status: fixed — the dispatcher selects a shared TLS transport with verification disabled only for hooks explicitly configured with `insecure_ssl=1`; address and redirect controls remain enforced

findings.finding: Hook fields read off a shared pointer outside the lock; the same race was recognised and fixed for one field only
findings.status: fixed — delivery queues receive a deep hook snapshot, including events and last response, captured under the store lock

findings.finding: A malformed body produces a successful empty response, so the runner fails later with an opaque error
findings.status: fixed — malformed JSON and incomplete action entries return 400 at the download-info boundary

findings.finding: Action tarball cache keyed by mutable ref, never invalidated, unbounded, holding full tarballs in memory
findings.status: fixed — cache identity is the resolved immutable commit SHA, returned bytes are detached, and insertion is bounded to 128 archives

findings.finding: Timeline attachments read and discarded — `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` content never appears anywhere
findings.status: fixed — bounded summary attachments persist with the job and render as safe Markdown in run detail

findings.finding: Unbounded `io.ReadAll` on log, artifact and scanning paths; the 4 MiB log cap is applied after the full read
findings.status: fixed — the remaining unbounded reads (secret-scanning blob scans in secret_scanning_ingest.go) now read through io.LimitReader capped at 5 MiB; the log/artifact/step-summary paths were already bounded by MaxBytesReader/LimitReader

findings.finding: `cancelTimeout` written without the store lock; watcher goroutines leak for runs that never resolve
findings.status: fixed — a dedicated mutex serializes watcher replacement/stop and replacing a watcher cancels the previous goroutine

findings.finding: Linear scans over every job and workflow on hot paths, never garbage collected — completed job messages holding plaintext secrets are retained indefinitely
findings.status: open

findings.finding: Secret values inserted into a regex mask unescaped, so a secret with metacharacters is rejected and left unmasked
findings.status: fixed — every literal token and secret is `regexp.QuoteMeta` encoded before entering the regex mask list

findings.finding: Matrix display names use sorted keys rather than declaration order, breaking required-status-check contexts
findings.status: fixed — YAML mapping order is retained and drives Cartesian expansion and display names

findings.finding: Include/exclude matching compares values via `fmt.Sprintf`, so `1` and `"1"` are equal
findings.status: fixed — normalized values are compared with type-preserving equality

findings.finding: Startup-failure runs emit no check suite and an empty conclusion; the merge gate's `startup_failure` branch is dead code
findings.status: fixed — jobless startup failures enqueue requested/completed lifecycle events, persist their suite id, and conclude the suite `startup_failure`

findings.finding: The dispatcher re-reads and re-parses every workflow file of every repository every minute; parse errors swallowed
findings.status: fixed — parse errors are now structured warnings with repository, file, cron, and timezone context; and the dispatcher no longer re-reads and re-parses every default-branch workflow every minute: a `scheduleIndex` cache holds each repo's parsed, cron-validated schedule keyed by the default-branch tip commit (`resolveRefSha`), rebuilt only when that tip moves (`buildScheduleIndex`), so a steady-state tick reduces to cron-matching against pre-parsed entries. The cache is pruned to live repos each tick (`retain`). Regression `TestScheduleIndexRebuildsOnlyOnTipChange` asserts one rebuild across two unchanged-tip ticks and a second rebuild after the tip advances

findings.finding: Any non-numeric version segment is silently treated as not vulnerable
findings.status: fixed — package-style prerelease/build identifiers participate in comparison and an unknown dialect fails safe by retaining the advisory rather than suppressing it

findings.finding: `runner.os`, `arch` and `name` are constants; the github context omits `workflow_ref` and `job_workflow_sha`, which are load-bearing for OIDC claims
findings.status: fixed — workflow/job workflow ref and SHA fields now reach the runner context, including reusable-workflow identity; and runner OS/architecture/name are now late-bound to the agent that actually leases the queued message: the job message is built runner-agnostically (`runnerContextData(nil)`) and the broker rewrites `contextData.runner` (os/arch/name plus OS-appropriate tool_cache/temp) to the leasing agent at delivery in `pullPendingMessage` (`rebindRunnerContext`, idempotent so a requeue rebinds afresh). OS/arch derive from the agent's self-reported labels, falling back to its OS description. Regressions `TestRunnerContextDerivedFromAgent` and `TestLeasedJobRebindsRunnerContext`

findings.finding: The cache download token — documented as the sole access control — is compared with `!=`; no eviction, and `LastAccessedAt` is faked
findings.status: fixed — constant-time token comparison and persisted restore-time `LastAccessedAt` landed earlier; finalizing a cache now enforces a per-repository budget (`maxRepoCacheBytes`, GitHub's 10 GiB default; a per-instance field so tests drive it small) via `evictRepoCacheOverLimit`, which deletes least-recently-used finalized entries (oldest `LastAccessedAt`, id breaking ties) until the repo is back under budget, byte-deletes outside the lock. LRU-order regression test

findings.finding: `ActionDownloadInfo` returned `"token": "x-access-token"` — the literal *username* half of the Basic credential, mistaken for the token — beside a hardcoded `"expiresAt": "2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"`, the same far-future placeholder another test in this package explicitly bans. The runner dutifully sent `Basic base64("x-access-token:x-access-token")`. The tarball route also read only Bearer, so a real token in the shape the runner sends would have been refused too
findings.status: fixed — the download info mints a job token for the plan the caller already authenticated as, with its real expiry, and the route accepts the Basic download credential as well as a Bearer job token. ACT-003's private-repository scoping is unchanged and now covered through the Basic form

findings.finding: `authenticateRunner` reports `missing runner bearer token` identically for an absent Authorization header and for one carrying a scheme it does not read, which is what made the tarball failure look like an anonymous request for two CI cycles
findings.status: fixed — absent, malformed and unsupported-scheme credentials are distinct failures with regression coverage

findings.finding: Actions Runner 2.336 signs its client assertion with PS256 while the server accepted only RS256, so the current official runner could register but not establish a session. Its bundled .NET 8.0.28 runtime also carries five fixed HIGH vulnerabilities, and replacing that runtime beneath the precompiled assemblies is binary-incompatible
findings.status: fixed — the assertion verifier accepts and independently verifies both PS256/PSS and legacy RS256/PKCS#1 signatures. Both runner images rebuild the immutable 2.336.0 source commit against the digest-pinned .NET 8.0.423 SDK and patched 8.0.29 runtime, with a fully content-hashed NuGet graph, then retain only the checksum-verified official scripts and Node runtimes around that rebuilt binary tree. The real runner harness pins registration, sessions, jobs, matrices, outputs, artifacts, cancellation, service containers and dispatcher-spawned ephemeral execution

findings.finding: The schedule dispatcher ran the per-minute scan inline on the ticker goroutine and recomputed the next boundary afterwards, so a scan overrunning a minute silently skipped every intervening minute's schedules
findings.status: fixed — the dispatcher threads a minute cursor and `fireSchedulesThrough` replays every whole minute in `(lastFired, now]`, bounded by a ten-minute catch-up and deduped by the per-minute firing claim; a regression drives a nine-minute overrun and asserts the skipped due minutes fire exactly once

findings.finding: A timezone'd schedule deduped its firing on the UTC minute, so a DST fall-back — the same wall-clock minute at two UTC instants — fired the workflow twice
findings.status: fixed — the claim is keyed on the reconstructed civil minute in the schedule's zone, collapsing both instants to one claim; a regression fires the two 01:30-local instants and asserts a single run

findings.finding: The firing claim was written before the run was created and never released, so a transient submit failure consumed the occurrence with no run and no retry
findings.status: fixed — `fireScheduledWorkflow` distinguishes transient failures and the caller releases the claim via `ReleaseScheduleFiring` so another replica or attempt can retry, while permanent conditions keep the claim; a regression re-claims a released firing

findings.finding: `fireScheduledWorkflow` re-fetched git storage with no nil guard and passed it to `resolveRefSha`, which dereferences a nil storer if a concurrent refresh dropped the entry
findings.status: fixed — a nil storer is logged and skipped before use

findings.finding: `PutBatch` is used at 4 call sites against 398 `MustPut` and 206 `MustDelete`; `DeleteRepo` alone issues 54 independent transactions
findings.status: partial — a batch executor commits a whole write set in one transaction. `DeleteRepo` stages its whole cascade in that transaction; the repository re-key on `RenameRepo`/`TransferRepo` now stages the repos row and every one of its ~40 subresource buckets (secrets, collaborators, teams, hooks, checks, workflows, commit statuses, notification read state, scanning alerts, packages, env secrets/variables, pages, …) into one `persistBatch` via a batch-aware `moveRepoKeyLocked`, so a crash can no longer split a repository across its old and new names; and `StarRepo`/`UnstarRepo`, `CreateOrg`, `RemoveMembership`, `DeleteLabel`/`DeleteMilestone`, `CreateOrgInvitation`, `AddRepoCollaborator`/`RemoveRepoCollaborator`, `CreateRepoDeployKey`/`DeleteRepoDeployKey`, `DeleteTeam` (with child re-parenting), `RemoveOutsideCollaborator`, `CancelOrgInvitation`, `DeleteEnterpriseCodeSecurityConfig` and `CreateSecretScanningPushProtectionBypass` each commit their whole multi-bucket mutation atomically. Org-invitation acceptance (`consumeOrgInvitationLocked` — every invited-team join plus the invitation removal) and expiry (`reconcileOrgInvitationsLocked` — the abandoned pending-membership drop plus the invitation-failed write) each now commit in one transaction, and `RenameBranch` re-keys the branch protection and writes the repo's default-branch change together. The classic and v2 project deletions commit their whole subtree in one transaction — `DeleteProject` (v2) with its fields/items/views, and `DeleteProjectClassic`/`DeleteProjectColumn` with their columns and cards via batch-aware `deleteProjectCard/ColumnBatchLocked` helpers — so a crash can no longer orphan a child pointing at a deleted parent. The pull-request reviewer and label mutations that emit one issue-event per element (`RequestReviewers`, `RemoveRequestedReviewers`, `AddPullRequestLabels`, `SetPullRequestLabels`, `ClearPullRequestLabels`, `RemovePullRequestLabel`) and the matching issue label and assignee mutations (`SetIssueLabels`, `ClearIssueLabels`, `AddIssueLabels`, `RemoveIssueLabel`, `AddIssueAssignees`, `RemoveIssueAssignees`) now commit every event with the pull-request/issue row in a single `persistBatch` via batch-aware `recordPullRequestEvent/LabelEventBatchLocked` and `recordIssueEventWithIDsBatchLocked`, so the timeline can no longer diverge from the reviewer/label/assignee state across a crash. A further sweep converts the credential and multi-bucket cascade mutations: user-to-server/refresh token create, revoke, rotate and grant-revoke; `RevokeCredentials` across all four token buckets; `DeleteOAuthApp` with all its issued tokens; classroom and classroom-assignment deletion with their assignments/acceptances; and the org-scoped delete cascades (`DeleteCodeSecurityConfiguration`, `DeleteCustomProperty`, `DeleteNetworkConfiguration`, `DeleteIssueField`, `handleDeleteOrganizationRole`) plus repo-invitation acceptance — each now a single `persistBatch`. Also converted: `CreateCheckRun` (inline suite + run), `PruneEnvironmentPolicies` (branch policies + protection rules), `persistTeamExternalGroupsLocked` (org groups + team binding) and `replaceOrganizationSCIMUser` (backing account + SCIM record, unlocking before any panic). Other multi-entity mutations still need transaction-by-transaction conversion (e.g. the multi-phase `renameGHESOrganization`)

findings.finding: Mutators change memory before persisting and `log.Fatalf` on failure — `os.Exit(1)` from a handler with the lock held and the mutation half-applied
