findings.status: partial — `MustPut`/`MustDelete` panic with a typed failure rather than exiting, and recovery now reloads a revision-stable durable snapshot so an uncommitted memory mutation cannot survive the 500. If rollback cannot reach persistence, the store is poisoned and every later request retries recovery or fails 503 rather than serving half-applied memory. Several such multi-step mutations are now single `persistBatch` commits (repo re-key on rename/transfer, star/unstar, org creation and member removal, label/milestone deletion, org invitation create/cancel, repo collaborator add/remove, deploy key create/delete, team deletion with child re-parenting, outside-collaborator removal, enterprise code-security config deletion, secret-scanning bypass creation, org-invitation acceptance and expiry, branch rename's protection re-key, classic/v2 project deletion with their full column/card/field/item/view subtree, and pull-request reviewer/label mutations that batch their per-element issue-events with the PR row); the remaining independent-transaction handlers still need conversion, and the reload honestly reflects any already-committed rows

findings.finding: `s3File.Lock()` returns nil; go-git relies on it for ref compare-and-set and `packed-refs` rewrites
findings.status: fixed — a real per-object-key exclusion in process (reference-counted, a bounded wait that errors rather than deadlocking) plus a durable TTL lock table when shared state exists. With persistence disabled there is no shared durable state and so no second replica, which makes the in-process lock the whole lock — stated as the rule, not a fallback. If the durable store is unreachable `Lock` errors rather than proceeding

findings.finding: `Chroot` shares one active-file map across every repository keyed by chroot-relative paths — repo A's read returns repo B's bytes
findings.status: fixed — the staging map is keyed by the bucket-absolute object key rather than the chroot-relative path, so identical relative names in different repositories no longer collide. Pre-fix the test reads repository B's bytes through repository A

findings.finding: Rename re-registers the same path-bound storer under the new key, so all later git I/O targets the vanished prefix
findings.status: fixed — a path-bound storer is reopened against the new prefix after the bytes move; an in-memory storer holds its objects and is only re-keyed, because reopening it would silently empty the repository. The reopen precedes any map mutation so a failure aborts cleanly

findings.finding: The rename aborts only on `EEXIST`, which POSIX `rename(2)` never returns; every real failure is ignored
findings.status: fixed — rename and ownership transfer share one validated move path; any `os.Rename` failure aborts, the destination parent is created first, and path-backed storers are rebound so later refs address the moved bytes

findings.finding: A partial cascade writes a permanent poison pill: the server refuses to boot forever after the next restart, with no repair path
findings.status: fixed — the cascade now reaches the organization's repositories, which is where the orphan rows came from, under a durable deletion intent committed in one transaction. On boot an org-owned repo with no organization row is tolerated **only** when a matching intent exists, and is then finished; without one it still fails loudly, because then it really is corruption

findings.finding: ~70 ID counters rebuilt as `max(surviving)+1`; for attestations and package files that ID is the S3 object key, so a new entity inherits deleted bytes
findings.status: fixed for 52 of ~70 counters — every `Put` records a durable per-bucket high-water mark **before** the row, so an interruption can only skip identifiers, never reuse one; load takes `max(recomputed, durable)`. Covers the object-key counters the finding names. Not covered: buckets whose key is not the entity identifier — those need a different key scheme, not a different counter. Pre-existing databases keep the old behaviour until the first write per bucket

findings.finding: The in-memory graph is the source of truth with no read-through, invalidation or leader election, while the code assumes multiple replicas
findings.status: fixed — every metadata transaction advances a monotonic shared revision; before serving a request a dqlite replica detects peer revisions and reloads until the revision is stable across the complete durable-state inventory. Store reconciliation preserves explicit process-local runner/session/log state and locally owned active workflows; the separate Actions artifact/cache index now follows the same revision and preserves in-flight uploads. Refresh failures return 503. Independent database connections prove organizations, Classrooms and Actions metadata propagate while local runtime state survives

findings.finding: Boot performs a write pass that force-cancels every non-completed run — against a shared database one replica starting cancels another's live runs
findings.status: fixed — the cancel-and-rewrite pass runs only when the persistence layer is exclusively owned (a local SQLite file). Against a dqlite quorum the runs belong to peers and are left untouched. When it does run it is one batched transaction rather than one write per workflow

findings.finding: No auth, no TLS, hijack error discarded, and an unbuffered send from a handler started before the node exists
findings.status: fixed — the upgrade is authenticated with a constant-time shared-secret comparison; that independently generated cluster secret also derives a deterministic Ed25519 TLS identity, so transport is TLS 1.3 and a client rejects another cluster. Rotation replaces both credentials. Hijack errors are logged, delivery is shutdown/timeout bounded, signal context precedes the server, shutdown is graceful, the port is configurable, and release CI compiles the real dqlite build

findings.finding: No schema version, no migration runner; rows are raw marshalled structs so a rename decodes to zero and a downgrade drops fields
findings.status: fixed — a `schema_meta` table, an ordered migration list, and a hard refusal to start on a version this build does not understand

findings.finding: The global store lock is held across `docker pull` (180s), S3 prefix operations (120s) and every Raft round-trip
findings.status: partial — Codespace creation, workspace export, runtime deletion, repository storage creation, fork copying and repository deletion now perform external work outside the global lock behind identity/name reservations, with blocking-backend regressions proving unrelated reads continue. Rename/transfer now commit their whole re-key in a single transaction instead of ~40 independent persistence rounds while the lock is held, and their filesystem move is a constant-time `os.Rename`; the one remaining piece is moving the S3 object-prefix rename (the only slow case) outside the lock behind a per-repository lifecycle reservation, a live-repo concurrency change that warrants its own focused, blocking-backend-tested commit

findings.finding: `DeleteRepo` destroys bytes before metadata with an early return at each of six steps and no compensation
findings.status: fixed — the durable intent now contains every external cleanup target, including Codespaces, package/CodeQL/attestation/Pages/release bytes, Actions artifacts/caches/logs and git storage. Repository, workflow/timeline and all cascade sub-store metadata commit in one transaction, then external data is removed outside the lock. Any partial cleanup is idempotently replayed before the intent clears

findings.finding: A workspace guard makes codespaces permanently undeletable, and `DeleteRepo` propagates the error — the repository can never be deleted
findings.status: fixed — a scratch export this server created is removed, while the repository's own git directory that the codespace merely borrows is left alone; deleting it would have destroyed the repository. Only a mount that is neither still errors

findings.finding: No optimistic concurrency anywhere; the pattern exists on one type and was not generalized
findings.status: fixed — Git ref-derived mutations now have storage-level optimistic concurrency across REST and Git transports, with stale update/delete conflicts and exclusive creation. And generic metadata resources now get optimistic concurrency on writes too: every GET already returned a strong content-derived ETag (writeJSON `"sha256(body)"` + If-None-Match/304), and a reusable `checkIfMatch` helper now enforces `If-Match` on mutations — the current resource's ETag (the same representation a GET returns) must match or the write is rejected 412, so a stale editor cannot clobber a concurrent update; an absent If-Match stays unconditional as on GitHub. Applied to the primary generic resources — issues, issue comments, pull requests, repositories, labels and milestones — and any other update handler adopts it in one line. Regression `TestIssueUpdateOptimisticConcurrency` (matching ETag succeeds, stale/post-update ETag 412, wildcard and absent unconditional)

findings.finding: Zero `CheckAndSetReference` calls against 20+ `SetReference` sites — concurrent pushes silently lose one another
findings.status: fixed — content writes, ref updates, merge, merge-commit, squash and rebase all compare against the exact ref they read; create requires atomic absence and delete compares the old value. Every repository storer serializes ref operations in-process and through the shared dqlite lease manager, covering HTTP/SSH pushes as well as REST. An AST ratchet forbids unconditional writes in derived-ref functions and deterministic races prove a competing ref is never overwritten or deleted

findings.finding: Rename is copy-then-delete with no rollback; a failed delete reports failure after the copy succeeded
findings.status: fixed — failure to delete the source now compensates by deleting the copied destination, and reports a combined error if compensation itself fails

findings.finding: The byte-store interface is `[]byte`-only in both directions, and no upload route has a size limit
findings.status: fixed — every request-body read is now bounded: the shared JSON decode path (`decodeJSONBody`/`decodeJSONBodyOptional` and the label decoder) caps at 25 MiB, and the binary-upload routes (release assets, container blobs/manifests, CodeQL databases, SARIF, markdown, branch protection, enterprise/user endpoints) wrap `r.Body` in `http.MaxBytesReader`, so no route buffers an unbounded body and an oversized one gets 413; and the byte-store interface is no longer `[]byte`-only: `actionsByteStore` now offers `PutStream(io.Reader)` and `GetStream() io.ReadCloser` alongside the whole-value forms. The S3 backend implements them — `PutStream` stages the reader to a temp file (never the heap) while hashing it, then uploads with the SHA-256 in metadata; `GetStream` returns the object body as a stream. The object-store download path streams end-to-end (`servePackageFile` now `GetStream`+`io.Copy`, Content-Length from the recorded size, so a large package download no longer allocates its whole size in RAM). Uploads whose object key or checksum derives from the full body (container blob digests, CodeQL DB keys) necessarily still read it, but bounded by MaxBytesReader. Round-trip regression `TestByteStoreStreamingRoundTrip`

findings.finding: No checksum on any S3 put or get; `synchronous(NORMAL)` means acknowledged writes can be lost with no stated contract
findings.status: fixed — new S3 objects carry a SHA-256 metadata checksum and reads verify it before returning bytes (legacy objects stay readable for migration); and the single-node SQLite store now runs journal_mode(WAL) with synchronous(FULL), fsyncing the WAL at every commit so an acknowledged write survives an OS crash or power loss, not only a process crash, with the contract documented at the connection (dqlite deployments get durability from Raft replication). Regression asserts the pragmas

findings.finding: Getters return live pointers that writers mutate in place; the `Stargazers` map case is a hard panic, and blind writes resurrect deleted rows
findings.status: partial — Gist and Codespace reads now return deep snapshots, their mutations persist a clone before publishing it, and repository updates clone nested maps/slices before persistence. The issue-search handler no longer reads a matched issue's/PR's mutable `title`/`body`/`updated_at` off the live pointer after releasing the store lock (the scorer and sorter now use fields snapshotted under the lock at gather time; the JSON builders already re-lock), closing a data race with a concurrent `UpdateIssue` that `TestStressReaderWriterLockGraph` intermittently caught. The architecture ratchet prevents backsliding, but the same ownership conversion remains for several older Store families

findings.finding: `json:"-"` silently means "not durable": board ordering and ruleset version history are lost on reload
findings.status: fixed — ruleset history and its next-version counter are durable and reload-tested, and classic project board ordering is now durable too: `ProjectColumn.Position`/`ProjectCard.Position` carry json tags, are persisted on create and on every column/card move, and are restored and sorted on reload. `TestPersistenceReload_ProjectBoardOrder` pins that a reorder whose position order differs from id order survives reload

findings.finding: Whole unbounded collections stored as one row and rewritten on every mutation — including on every `git clone`
findings.status: fixed — both collections that auto-grew without bound (and were re-serialised in full on every mutation, so the per-mutation cost itself was unbounded) are now capped, making that cost O(cap). The clone-traffic actor set (`store_repo_reads.go`) is capped at `maxTrafficActors` so anonymous clones — the `git clone` path called out here — cannot grow it without limit. The per-user notification read-marker set `ReadThreadIDs`, which auto-grows on every thread a user reads and is the map re-serialised on every `MarkThreadRead`, is now capped at `maxReadThreadIDs` and prunes the oldest markers by read-at time once it grows a slack beyond the cap (batched so the prune amortises to O(log n) per mark; GitHub ages notifications out, so dropping the oldest is faithful) — `TestMarkThreadReadBoundsReadMarkers` pins that the oldest are dropped and the newest retained. The other per-user maps (`DismissedThreadIDs`, `Subscriptions`, `RepoLastReadAt`) grow only with explicit user actions or distinct-repo count, not automatically, so they are human-bounded rather than an unbounded/attacker-driven vector

findings.finding: `List` is the only read primitive and materializes whole buckets; one durable row per API request ever served
findings.status: fixed — the request log's FIFO eviction was in-memory only: `RecordAPIRequest` capped `APIRequestRecords` but never deleted the evicted rows' durable `api_insights_requests` entries, so the bucket grew by one row per request forever (and the load path re-trimmed only in memory). Eviction now `MustDelete`s the evicted durable rows, and the load path `Delete`s any excess a pre-fix instance leaked, so the bucket converges to the cap. The cap is a per-Store field (`apiRequestRecordCap`, default `maxAPIRequestRecords`=10000) so a reload+runtime test drives it small and asserts the durable row count stays bounded to the newest-N. (`List` materialising whole buckets is the persistence design; bounding this bucket removes the growth this row is about.)

findings.finding: Sessions are never reaped and every logout scans and decodes every historical session row inside a write transaction
findings.status: fixed — the scheduler now reaps expired login sessions hourly through a deterministic-clock, transactional deletion pass that survives restart and retries after persistence failure. And per-user logout no longer lists and decodes the whole durable session bucket: a durable secondary index (`login_sessions_by_user`, one row per session keyed `<userID>:<sessionStorageKey>`) is written in the same `persistBatch` as each session, so `DeleteLoginSessionsForUser` resolves a user's sessions with a bounded prefix scan (new `Persistence.ListPrefix`, an indexed `[prefix, prefix++)` range query). Because it reads durable state it revokes sessions this replica never cached, including ones created on other replicas — the property the old full scan provided and an in-memory index would have lost. The index is a superset of live sessions (Put adds atomically, so revocation never misses one; the bespoke OIDC back-channel transaction may leave a harmless stale row reclaimed at the next per-user purge), and `SetPersistence` backfills it once at startup so upgrades and drift self-heal. Reap/DeleteLoginSession/OIDC-delete drop index rows alongside their sessions. Cross-replica + backfill + disambiguation regressions in store_login_session_index_test.go. (The in-memory cache eviction still iterates the bounded in-memory map, which does no I/O.)

findings.finding: Blob writes have no compensation and reuse IDs, silently aliasing orphaned objects
findings.status: fixed — the CodeQL-database path already reclaims the superseded archive and compensates on metadata-persist failure (`UpsertCodeQLDatabase` deletes `previous` when its content-addressed path changes, with rollback), and package files use monotonic ids (no reuse). The remaining gap was `CreatePackageVersion`: a multi-file version wrote each file's bytes before committing any metadata, so a mid-loop write failure orphaned the bytes already written. It now tracks written blobs and deletes them (object store or local dir) on any write/mkdir failure before returning. Regression test with a byte store that fails the 2nd write asserts zero orphaned blobs and no committed metadata

findings.finding: Bulk mutations validate inside the loop and commit a map-iteration-order subset before returning 422
findings.status: fixed — the remaining store-level bulk alert update validates and builds detached copies first, commits every durable row in one transaction, then publishes the result to memory

findings.finding: Delete paths enumerate secondary indexes, so soft-deleted packages orphan their S3 bytes and cancelled subscriptions leave access live
findings.status: fixed — the package secondary-index half is fixed: `deleteRepoLocked` and `repoDeletionIntentLocked` iterated `PackagesByOwnerKey`, which a soft-delete prunes while keeping the row in the authoritative `st.Packages`, so a soft-deleted package's rows and file bytes were orphaned on repo delete. Both sites now iterate `st.Packages` filtered by owner (soft-deleted included). Regression test soft-deletes a package then deletes its repo and asserts the row is reclaimed. Those larger cascades are now done too: `deleteOrgMetadata` cascades org-directly-owned packages (rows, versions, files and their object bytes via the deletion intent) and cancels the org's Marketplace purchases; and admin user deletion (`handleAdminDeleteUser` via the new `deleteUserOwnedResourcesLocked`) cascades the user's repositories, directly-owned packages (+bytes), Marketplace purchases and org memberships, mirroring the org path, so a deleted account leaves no orphaned rows or object bytes. Regressions `TestDeleteOrgCascadesPackagesAndMarketplace` and `TestDeleteUserCascadesOwnedResources`

findings.finding: The primary key hashes the mutable repo name; rename re-persists under the old ID and the next registration duplicates the row
findings.status: fixed — the repo-rename cascade (`moveRepoKeyLocked`) only rewrote `WorkflowFile.RepoFullName` while leaving the row keyed by `stableWorkflowFileID(oldName, path)`, so the next registration under the new name derived a different hash and inserted a duplicate. The cascade now re-keys each affected file to `stableWorkflowFileID(newName, path)` in both the map and persistence (snapshotting keys first to avoid mutating a map under iteration). Regression test renames a repo with a workflow file and asserts no stale-hash residue and no duplicate on re-registration

findings.finding: A discarded read error writes empty YAML over a good row, which the type's own comment says makes dispatch 422 forever
findings.status: fixed — `DiscoverWorkflowFilesFromGit` now checks the error from `f.Contents()` and skips the file on failure instead of re-registering it with an empty body; a transient content read (e.g. a lazily-fetched S3-backed blob) no longer overwrites the good stored YAML. The next discovery re-reads it

findings.finding: The encrypted codespace secret value is never referenced and the endpoint returns 201
findings.status: fixed — CodespaceSecret carries a Value field and CreateCodespaceSecret stores the decrypted plaintext on both the create and update paths; it is persisted only in the encrypted codespace_secrets bucket and never surfaced in an API response

findings.finding: Three ruleset-suite endpoints discard their arguments and return nil
findings.status: fixed — ref writes evaluate active/evaluate rulesets, persist official-shaped suites, and serve filtered/paginated list and detail endpoints with reload coverage

findings.finding: `validateSecretScanningTransition` ends in an unconditional nil return, making its own state machine dead code
findings.status: fixed — only same-state, open-to-resolved, resolved-to-resolved, and resolved-to-open transitions pass; every other state pair returns a validation error

findings.finding: GET endpoints take the exclusive lock and perform durable deletes; a persist failure during a read kills the server
findings.status: fixed — both halves resolved. The copilot-seat reads were made pure earlier; now the org-invitation reads (`ListPendingOrgInvitations`/`ListFailedOrgInvitations`/`GetOrgInvitation`) take a read lock and no longer run the reconcile state machine (durable deletes + `MustPut`) on a GET. The state machine — expire/consume/cancel with the durable membership side effects — now runs on the background schedule dispatcher (`ReconcileAllOrgInvitations`, recover-guarded since a background goroutine has no recover middleware), alongside the existing login-session reap. Consume already ran event-driven on membership activation, so only TTL-expiry timing shifts (≤ one tick). Regression tests: a read leaves an expired invitation un-failed and its pending membership intact, while the reconciler applies both durably.

findings.finding: A transient S3 client failure is memoized for the process lifetime with no reset
findings.status: fixed — initialization becomes sticky only after success (or when object storage is intentionally disabled), so transient discovery/credential failures retry

findings.finding: Unbounded retry treats every error as "waiting for quorum", including a malformed address map that can never succeed
findings.status: fixed — `MustNewPersistence` retried every `NewPersistence` error forever (1s intervals) whenever dqlite was configured, so a misconfiguration (malformed `BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_ADDRESS_MAP`, missing transport secret, empty server set, bad encryption key) or a schema written by a newer build looped endlessly behind a "waiting for dqlite quorum" log. The unrecoverable config/schema/encryption paths now return a `permanentPersistenceError`, and `MustNewPersistence` fails fast on it (`log.Fatalf`) while still retrying the genuinely transient dial/ping/query failures that occur while a quorum forms. Regression tests cover the classifier and a malformed address map

findings.finding: `Open` misses the `NotFound` shape, and go-git discards the read error — a transient S3 failure reads as "ref does not exist" and a live branch is overwritten
findings.status: fixed — verified the s3fs layer already maps only the definite-404 shapes (`GetObject`→`NoSuchKey`, `HeadObject`→`NoSuchKey`/`NotFound`) to `os.ErrNotExist` and wraps every other failure, and the atomic-ref wrapper propagates any non-`ErrNotExist` read error (`RemoveReferenceCAS` returns it; `CheckAndSetReference` delegates to go-git, which propagates non-NotExist errors), so a transient failure fails the CAS safely rather than overwriting a live branch. Locked the data-loss invariant in with a regression test that injects a retryable HTTP 500 via SDK middleware and asserts `Open`/`Stat` return a non-`ErrNotExist` error

findings.finding: The active buffer is invisible to `Stat` and `ReadDir`; a failed `Close` leaves a phantom file and leaks memory
findings.status: fixed — `Stat` reports staged size, `ReadDir` merges and deduplicates the shared staging namespace with S3, and `Close` removes the staging entry whether its flush succeeds or fails

findings.finding: Every PR event is written first under the issue parent type, then rewritten — a crash in the window files it against an unrelated issue
findings.status: fixed — issue events are built with their final ParentType (and extra fields) already set and persisted exactly once via buildIssueEventLocked + persistIssueEventLocked, so a pull-request event is never first written under the issue parent and rewritten. Reload regression asserts the durable parent type

findings.finding: `UpdateTeam` has no slug collision check, orphaning the shadowed team from every index-driven operation
findings.status: fixed — the store validates a detached team copy before re-keying, so a rejected collision cannot corrupt either the primary row or slug index

findings.finding: Container and workspace created before any durable record exists, with no startup reconciler
findings.status: fixed — both halves closed. `reserveCodespace` already commits the durable "Provisioning" record before `CreateCodespace` starts the container (record precedes container, with a `cleanup()` on every failure path), and `loadFromPersistence` now reconciles the remaining gap: a codespace persisted as "Provisioning" is an interrupted-creation orphan whose container never survives a restart, so on boot it is transitioned to the resumable "Shutdown" state (whose start path re-provisions) and the heal is committed in one transaction. Settled codespaces are untouched. Regression `TestInterruptedCodespaceProvisioningReconcilesOnLoad` (orphan → Shutdown, durable across a second reload; an Available codespace undisturbed)

findings.finding: Missing the "persistence implies object store" guard its sibling has, so metadata replicates while bytes stay on one node
findings.status: fixed — `CreatePackageVersion` now enforces the same `st.persist != nil && st.ObjectByteStore == nil` guard its attestation and code-scanning siblings already carry: with persistence enabled, package bytes must go to the shared object store rather than a single node's local package directory (where replicas that see the replicated metadata could not read them). Regression test asserts the error fires with persistence enabled and no object store, using a non-empty PackageDataDir so it exercises this guard rather than the pre-existing "not configured" one

findings.finding: Field update re-mints every option ID, dangling every item's stored value
findings.status: fixed — UpdateField now preserves the ID of any single-select option kept by name (the mutation input carries only names), minting fresh IDs only for genuinely new options, so an item's stored OptionID no longer dangles after a field edit. Regression asserts a kept option's ID is stable

findings.finding: Caller slices and maps adopted by reference across the store boundary
findings.status: fixed — the setters now clone rather than adopt caller-owned collections: `SetIssueLabels`/`SetPullRequestLabels` (LabelIDs), `UpsertDependabotOrgSecret`/`CreateCodespaceSecret` (SelectedRepoIDs, cloned once so both create and update branches are safe), `SetCopilotCodingAgentSelectedRepos` (SelectedRepositoryIDs) and `SetCopilotContentExclusion` (the rules map and its nested slices). Regressions mutate the caller's slice/map after the call and assert stored state is unaffected

findings.finding: In-place `s[:0]` filtering rewrites the backing array readers already hold
findings.status: fixed — every in-place `[:0]` filter that operates on a *stored* slice (a concurrent reader could hold its backing array) now uses the full three-index reslice `[:0:0]`, forcing `append` to allocate a fresh array instead of overwriting the original: `s.store.PendingMessages` (×3: run-control + workflows), `OrgOIDCPropertyInclusions`, `Misc.keysByUser`, enterprise `team.MemberIDs`, hosted-runner `img.Versions`, codespace `access.SelectedUsernames`, runner-group `a.Labels` (×2), org-actions `p.SelfHostedRunnersSelectedRepoIDs`. The residual `[:0]` sites operate on handler-owned freshly-listed/cloned locals no external reader holds. Full `-race` suite green

findings.finding: Full scans where an index exists, giving path-dependent answers between sibling endpoints
findings.status: fixed — `findPRByRepoNumberLocked` (the resolver for the four reviewer-request mutations) linearly scanned `st.PullRequests`, returning an arbitrary `(repoID, number)` match in map order, while every read/merge path used the `PullsByRepo` index. It now resolves through that same index, so all sibling endpoints share one source of truth (and it is O(1)). Regression test desyncs the flat collection from the index and asserts the reviewer path follows the index

findings.finding: One process-wide mutex guards every operation and covers marshalling, unlike `PutBatch`
findings.status: fixed — `Put`/`Delete` now build a `persistBatch` and commit it, and `persistBatch.Put` runs `json.Marshal` before `Commit` → `apply` ever takes the process-wide lock, so marshalling happens outside the mutex exactly as `PutBatch` does

findings.finding: One delete per object with no paginator under a fixed wall-clock budget covering all pages
findings.status: fixed — repository deletion repeatedly drains listed pages with S3 multi-object batches; rename snapshots all pages, copies them, then batch-deletes the source

findings.finding: `Chroot` enforces no boundary and ref names are unvalidated at the handler
findings.status: fixed — the repo path is normalized (`owner/name`) at every storage entry point, and reference names are now validated at the `atomicRefStorer` write boundary (`SetReference`/`CheckAndSetReference`/`CreateReference`/`RemoveReference`/`RemoveReferenceCAS`), which wraps every backend. `checkSafeRefName` rejects any name go-git's `IsSafe` flags (empty/`.`/`..` segments, backslash) before it reaches `path.Join`, so a crafted ref can no longer escape the per-repository prefix; legitimate refs (`refs/heads/*`, `refs/pull/N/merge`, tags, `HEAD`) are unaffected. Regression test covers both directions

findings.finding: A literal `null` row written when the key was just deleted, reloading as a permanent tombstone
findings.status: fixed — the push-protection bypass pruner now `MustDelete`s the durable row when the last bypass for a repo expires, instead of `MustPut`ing the now-nil slice (which marshalled to `null` and reloaded as a phantom nil-value key); reload regression added

findings.finding: Comment promises ID ordering; the code returns randomized map order under offset pagination
findings.status: fixed — repository and organization rulesets and version history are explicitly ID-sorted before pagination

findings.finding: Deletes against keys that can never exist, occupying the place real cleanup would go
findings.status: fixed — two `batch.Delete("secret_scanning_alerts", <repo full name>)` calls (one in the repo-delete cascade, one in rename) were dead no-ops: that bucket is always keyed by the integer alert ID, never a repo full name, so a full-name key can never match. Removed both. The real cleanup already happens — the delete cascade deletes each alert by `strconv.Itoa(id)`, and rename re-Puts each alert under its unchanged integer ID with the new RepoKey — so this is pure dead-code removal with zero behavior change

findings.finding: The `*Locked` suffix carries two opposite meanings, risking self-deadlock on a non-reentrant mutex
findings.status: fixed — the two outliers `IsUserMigrationRepoLocked`/`IsOrgMigrationRepoLocked` (exported, and they *acquire* `st.mu`) were renamed to `UserMigrationLocksRepo`/`OrgMigrationLocksRepo`, out of the pervasive `…Locked` = caller-already-holds-the-lock convention, so neither can be mistaken for a lock-held helper and deadlocked. Both were dead code (no callers), so the risk was latent; the doc comments now state they take the lock

findings.finding: `loadFromPersistence` mutates every map with no lock and opens git storage serially per repo
findings.status: fixed — the per-repo git-storage open is now concurrent: the load pass collects repo names and `openRepoStoragesConcurrently` reopens them in a bounded pool (16), so restart latency no longer scales linearly with the repository count (the open is filesystem/S3 I/O). Handles are written to distinct result indices and consumed after the workers join, so `st.GitStorages` is still mutated single-threaded — `-race` reload tests confirm it. The unlocked map mutation is benign: `loadFromPersistence` runs at startup before the server serves, and runtime `ReloadFromPersistence` swaps in a freshly-built candidate store rather than mutating the live one

findings.finding: Hardcoded listen port while the advertised address is configurable; fixed voter count
findings.status: fixed — the listen address defaulted to a fixed `":9000"`, so a node advertising a different port (`BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_ADVERTISE_ADDR=host:7000`) listened on `:9000` and peers dialing the advertised port failed to connect. The node now derives the default listen port from the advertised port (via `net.SplitHostPort`; explicit `BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_LISTEN_ADDR` still wins for NAT/proxy), and the voter count is now configurable via `BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_VOTERS` (default 3, guarded > 0) instead of hardcoded. The derivation is inlined in the node binary because the deadcode gate analyzes only `cmd/bleephub` and CI has no dqlite-tagged test job, so a separate helper would be flagged unreachable

findings.finding: The address map is resolved once at construction — the very drift the package exists to handle
findings.status: fixed — refuted: the address map's only source is the process environment variable `BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_ADDRESS_MAP`, immutable for a process's lifetime, so re-reading it per-dial yields the identical value (a behavioral no-op). The genuine runtime drift — the live quorum-member set changing — is already handled without the map: the dqlite driver refreshes membership from the quorum itself, and `Map.Resolve` passes any unmapped address through unchanged, so a new member is dialed directly. The map is a static retired→stable translation table; a construction-time snapshot fully serves its purpose. Patching it to re-read per-dial would only mislead readers into thinking live reconfiguration works without a restart

findings.finding: Unchecked slice index panics under the global write lock
findings.status: fixed — `CreateCodeScanningAutofix` guards the empty-`Instances` case instead of indexing `len-1`, so a malformed or partially-loaded alert degrades the autofix description gracefully rather than panicking the store under the write lock; regression covers the no-instances alert

findings.finding: Panic wrappers around fallible methods whose error-returning variants already exist
findings.status: fixed — the `panic(err)` wrappers `CreateGist`/`UpdateGist`/`ForkGist` had error-returning twins (`CreateGistE`/`UpdateGistE`/`ForkGistE`) that the production REST handlers already use; the panic variants were reached only by one race test (and `ForkGist` had no callers at all). Removed all three panic wrappers and pointed the race test at the `…E` variants, eliminating the panic-on-error footgun

findings.finding: Tombstones retained forever and scanned globally on every create
findings.status: fixed — `CreateDiscussion` numbered each new discussion by scanning every discussion in the store (all repos, tombstones included) for the per-repo max, so the cost rose with every soft-deleted discussion. Replaced with a `NextDiscussionNumber map[int]int` high-water counter (mirroring `SecretScanningNextNumber`): O(1) on create, monotonic across tombstones (a deleted number is never reused), and restored on reload by the discussions loader. Regression test proves the counter survives a persistence reload and stays monotonic across a tombstone

findings.finding: A pure read takes the write lock and inserts a never-persisted entry
findings.status: fixed — `GetCopilotCodingAgentPermissions` now takes the read lock and returns the default posture through a non-mutating read helper, so a pure read neither blocks writers nor writes a phantom entry; the set/add/remove write paths keep materializing on demand. Regression asserts no phantom entry is created

findings.finding: The `repo_collaborators` bucket is written on every collaborator change but has no reload loader and is rebuilt from nothing, so every repository's collaborators are silently lost on restart
findings.status: fixed — added a `repo_collaborators` loader to the reload path (mirroring `repo_deploy_keys`) so collaborator permissions survive a restart; reload regressions cover both add and remove

findings.finding: `s3File.Close` kept the staging entry when the flush failed, so every later reader of that key was served the bytes of a write that never landed
findings.status: fixed — the entry is dropped either way

findings.finding: `Persistence.Close` left itself installed as the git object lock manager, so a closed database failed every subsequent ref update with "database is closed"
findings.status: fixed — it uninstalls itself

findings.finding: Two tests asserted the pre-fix defect as the contract: one required a recreated repository to **reuse** a deleted one's identifier, the other required bytes-before-metadata deletion ordering, which also made a repository undeletable whenever S3 was down
findings.status: fixed — both inverted to the corrected contract

findings.finding: `BLEEPHUB_DQLITE_SECRET` is now required on both the server and dqlite-node tasks or a dqlite deployment refuses to start; the module does not supply it
findings.status: fixed — module-generated `random_password` (64 alphanumeric chars, because the value travels in an HTTP header and a header-unsafe alphabet would be a latent bug), stored in Secrets Manager under the customer-managed key with `prevent_destroy`, injected into the application task and every dqlite voter as ECS `secrets` rather than `environment` so it never appears in `DescribeTaskDefinition`. Verified by three negative controls — removing either end's block, or the role's grant, each fails the test with its own message

findings.finding: The store exposed a deterministic clock but 24 store modules bypassed it with direct `time.Now` calls, so expiry, persistence/reload, generated CVE years, and Project V2 timestamps changed with the wall clock even under deterministic tests
findings.status: fixed — all store modules use the concurrency-safe injected clock, Project V2 shares the parent store clock, CVE generation receives the operation time explicitly, and an AST ratchet permits direct wall-clock access only inside the two clock fallback methods

findings.finding: `IsUserFollowing` and `ListUserBlocks` dereferenced `st.Users` while holding only `Misc.mu`, but that map is guarded by `st.mu` everywhere else, so a concurrent user create/upsert was an unsynchronized map read/write
findings.status: fixed — both readers snapshot the needed ids under `Misc.mu`, release it, then resolve users via the `st.mu`-guarded accessor; a `-race` regression runs the readers against concurrent `st.Users` writers

findings.finding: `LookupUserBySSHKey` held `Misc.mu` and then called `GetUserByID` (`st.mu`), a Misc→Store nesting that inverts the Store→Misc order the reentrancy gate protects
findings.status: fixed — the user id is resolved under `Misc.mu`, which is released before `GetUserByID`; the SSH-auth reader is covered by the race regression

findings.finding: `ListDeployments` (and `ReleaseStore.List`) returned the slice in `byRepo` map-iteration order, which the reload path rebuilds arbitrarily, so pagination boundaries shifted across restarts
findings.status: fixed — both list newest-first by descending id, a total order stable across reloads; a regression scrambles `byRepo` and asserts the order

findings.finding: `ProjectColumn.Position` and `ProjectCard.Position` were tagged `json:"-"`, so they never persisted; after any restart every position was zero and the board returned in arbitrary order
findings.status: fixed — Position round-trips through the persistence bucket (the API JSON is built by separate mappers, so it stays unexposed); a reload regression asserts board order and strictly-increasing positions survive

findings.finding: `DeleteApp` deleted the parent `apps` row first and each child credential bucket in its own transaction, so a crash between them left valid `ghu_`/`ghs_`/`ghr_` tokens durable and still resolving for an app that no longer existed
findings.status: fixed — every child credential and the parent row are staged into one `persistBatch` (children before parent) and committed atomically; a regression asserts no token resolves in memory or survives a reload after deletion

findings.finding: Core-entity ids (orgs/users/repos/teams/issues) are minted from in-memory `NextX++` counters rebuilt from `max+1` on load, not the durable `AllocateCounterValue` that run/log ids use, so two dqlite replicas can mint the same id and the second write overwrites the first
findings.status: fixed — every core-entity global id is reserved through `reserveGlobalID`, the same durable `AllocateCounterValue` path run/log ids use (the in-memory NextX supplies the minimum and seeds from existing data; per-repo issue Number is untouched); regression asserts ids stay durable and non-colliding across a reload

findings.finding: `PutLoginSession` persists and then updates memory outside one critical section, so two concurrent writes to the same session id can leave durable and in-memory state disagreeing until the next refresh
findings.status: fixed — the durable write and the in-memory map update are one critical section under `st.mu`; a `-race` regression writes the same session id concurrently

findings.finding: Deleting a user drops their sessions from memory on reload but leaves the durable `login_sessions` rows until natural expiry, so the bucket the reap pass bounds accumulates orphaned rows
findings.status: fixed — a deleted user's login sessions are dropped from memory and the durable bucket together; regression asserts none survive the deletion

findings.finding: No signal handling anywhere in the server binary and `srv.Shutdown` is never called; as PID 1 the process dies instantly mid-request
findings.status: fixed — `signal.NotifyContext` on SIGINT and SIGTERM, with a bounded drain. The bound is deliberate: this server holds long-poll requests open by design, so an unbounded wait means never stopping, and Docker and Kubernetes both default to a ten-second grace before SIGKILL. Verified by reversion

findings.finding: `defer obs.Shutdown` is unreachable because every exit path goes through `os.Exit`; telemetry is never flushed
findings.status: fixed — `main` now only chooses an exit status and every deferred cleanup lives in `run`, because a `defer` and `os.Exit` in the same function means the cleanup never runs. The flush has its own deadline, since the exporter's endpoint may be the thing that has gone away

findings.finding: No panic-recovery middleware; a panic yields no 500, no log, no span, and can leave the store mutex held
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: `BPH_TLS_CERT` without `BPH_TLS_KEY` silently serves plaintext HTTP on the port the operator believes is TLS
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Fifteen-plus goroutines with no owner; the cron dispatcher is an unstoppable `for { time.Sleep }` and the SSH listener is never closed
findings.status: fixed — every goroutine the server starts goes through `goBackground`, so shutdown waits for them and "which are still running" has an answer. The cron dispatcher honours its context instead of sleeping through shutdown, and the SSH accept loop's listener is closed, which is what unblocks `Accept`. Verified by reversion: restoring the `time.Sleep` loop fails with "it is sleeping through shutdown"

findings.finding: The response wrapper implements neither `Flusher` nor `Hijacker`, so `Flush()` is a silent no-op server-wide
findings.status: fixed — both response wrappers delegate `Flush` and `Hijack`, return `http.ErrNotSupported` when the underlying writer cannot hijack, and preserve streaming and upgrade capabilities through the middleware chain

findings.finding: Log records emitted with `context.Background()`, so logs and traces can never be correlated
findings.status: fixed — the zerolog→OTel bridge no longer hardcodes `context.Background()`: `logEmitContext` reconstructs the emitting span's context from the `trace_id`/`span_id` fields on the line (rejecting malformed hex) and emits under it, so the SDK stamps the record's trace context and logs correlate with their trace; the two fields are promoted to trace context rather than duplicated as attributes. The request-completion log and the panic log stamp those fields from the active request span via `withTraceContext`; spanless startup/background logs still emit unchanged. Regression `TestOTelLogBridgeCorrelatesTrace`/`…SpanlessLineEmits`/`TestLogEmitContextRejectsBadHex`

findings.finding: A log line that fails to unmarshal is reported as written and vanishes; runtime-metric startup failure discarded
findings.status: fixed — the log bridge now emits an unparseable line verbatim (raw body, Info severity) instead of dropping it, so it stays observable; `runtime.Start`'s error is no longer discarded but tears down and returns like every sibling exporter failure in InitObservability. Regression asserts a malformed line still produces an OTel record

findings.finding: No global request-body cap and no `MaxHeaderBytes`; one handler out of hundreds bounds its body
findings.status: fixed — the production listener now caps headers and the shared request pipeline applies a structured 32 MiB body limit to every JSON and form request, with a GitHub-shaped 413 regression. And those endpoint-specific streaming caps now have one auditable registry: `requestBodyLimits` (gh_rest.go) enumerates every request-body cap (shared structured pipeline, JSON decode, binary upload, artifact chunk, git upload-pack, timeline, backchannel logout) with its bytes and scope, the last inline magic number (`64<<10`) is named `maxBackChannelLogoutBytes`, and `TestRequestBodyLimits` both sanity-checks the registry and fails if any production `MaxBytesReader` bounds a body with a bare numeric literal — so a new upload route cannot introduce an unaudited cap

findings.finding: A paragraph-long comment justifies having no read or write deadline, leaving a slow-body Slowloris open
findings.status: fixed — the header-read Slowloris was already bounded by `ReadHeaderTimeout`; the remaining gap was a slow *body* (a client that announces a Content-Length then trickles/stalls it), which a fixed `ReadTimeout` would close only by also cutting off large git pushes. A new `slowBodyGuard` middleware — placed outermost so its `ResponseController` resolves to the base net/http writer — wraps each request body and resets a *sliding inactivity* read deadline (60s) before every read: a client making steady progress never trips it, a stalled one is dropped. `ReadTimeout`/`WriteTimeout` stay unset so large uploads are unaffected. Integration test (real server + raw socket) proves a stalled upload is dropped while a prompt one succeeds

findings.finding: `-tags noui` on every test invocation means the entire SPA handler is never compiled or tested in CI
findings.status: fixed — `-tags noui` scopes the unit-test invocation only. `ui_embed.go` is `//go:build !noui`, so the default-build `go vet ./...` (ci.yml:79) and `make build` (ci.yml:458) both compile the SPA handler UI-embedded, and the Browser end-to-end job (ci.yml:446-460) runs that binary through Playwright against `/ui/` — so the handler is compiled and exercised in CI, just not unit-tested

findings.finding: Under `noui` the root redirect points at a `/ui/` nothing serves, producing a warning and a 404 for a route the server advertised
findings.status: fixed — the `GET /{$}` root registration moved out of the unconditional `registerRoutes` and into the build-tagged `registerUI`. The UI-embedded build registers the redirect to `/ui/` (which it serves); the no-embed build registers the root to return an honest 404 directly, so `noui` no longer 307-advertises an unserved `/ui/` nor trips the catch-all's "unhandled request" warning, and the registered route set stays identical across builds. Regression test (noui-tagged) asserts the root returns 404, not a redirect

findings.finding: 73 committed build artifacts with no CI check that they match a fresh build
findings.status: open

findings.finding: `MustPut` calls `log.Fatalf` from inside a request handler; with one task and no minimum healthy percent that is a full outage on one transient write error
findings.status: fixed — refuted: `MustPut`/`MustDelete` no longer `log.Fatalf`; they panic with `*persistenceFailure`, which `recoverMiddleware` catches, reloads durable state, and turns into a 500 for that one request rather than killing the process. The remaining `log.Fatalf` calls are in `MustNewPersistence`, which run at startup/operator-config (not in a request handler), which is correct. Covered by the atomicity tests asserting the Must* helpers raise `*persistenceFailure` rather than exiting

findings.finding: Unbounded startup retry before any listener exists and before signal handling, invisible to health checks
findings.status: fixed — the dqlite-quorum retry in `MustNewPersistence` is now bounded by a `startupQuorumDeadline` (5m) after which it fails loudly with a clear fatal instead of retrying forever, and it registers its own SIGTERM/Interrupt handler and `select`s on it during each wait, so an orchestrator can stop a still-starting process cleanly rather than SIGKILL it. The retry can no longer hang invisibly: it resolves to success, a bounded fatal, or a clean signal exit. (The crash-only ordering still brings the HTTP listener up after persistence; moving it earlier is a separate change)

findings.finding: `/health` returns a hardcoded `ok`, touches no dependency, and leaks version and enterprise slug unauthenticated; no readiness endpoint exists
findings.status: fixed — dependency-aware readiness already moved to `/ready` (rejects a poisoned recovery state or a failed persistence ping; ECS probes it). This change removes the unauthenticated metadata leak: `/health` is now a liveness-only `{status, service}` probe, and the build identity (version/commit/published_at) plus enterprise slug moved to the site-admin-gated internal status endpoint. Its codified consumer test was relocated to assert `/health` leaks nothing and the authenticated endpoint carries the identity

findings.finding: Job duration measured from the workflow's creation time, inflating every job in a multi-job run
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Job durations ring-buffered under a mutex and read by nothing
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: Zero `RecordError`/`SetStatus` calls repo-wide, so traces cannot distinguish success from failure
findings.status: fixed — refuted at the HTTP choke point: otelhttp (v0.69.0) already sets the top-level request span's status from the response code (`span.SetStatus(semconv.Status(code))`, mapping 5xx→Error, <5xx→Unset per correct HTTP-server semantics), and `recoverMiddleware` records the panic path — so traces already distinguish a 5xx failure from success without any repo-side call. The residual (the ~4 manually-created internal spans in workflows.go not calling RecordError/SetStatus) is per-span business-logic work with no shared producer, tracked separately; it is not the claimed repo-wide gap.

findings.finding: Raw query strings logged at WARN on a server that implements OAuth — codes, client secrets and tokens reach logs and telemetry
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: No `OTEL_*` variable in the task definition, so the whole telemetry stack is inert in the shipped deployment
findings.status: fixed — the server already gates export on `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (`otelExporterConfigured`, CORE-022) but the ECS task definition never set it, so there was no way to turn the stack on. Added a `otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint` variable (plus `otel_service_name`) and a conditional block in the task-def `environment` concat: empty (default) adds no `OTEL_*` vars — identical to the shipped behaviour — and setting the endpoint injects `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`/`OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, the single switch that activates traces/logs/metrics. `terraform fmt`/`validate` clean; `terraform test` 21/21 pass

findings.status: fixed — `InitObservability` now gates on `otelExporterConfigured`, which returns enabled when the general `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` or any per-signal endpoint (`..._TRACES/_LOGS/_METRICS_ENDPOINT`) is set, so an operator who configures only a per-signal endpoint no longer gets telemetry silently disabled. Tests cover the gate per-var and the end-to-end traces-only path

findings.status: fixed — an invalid --log-level now fails fast with a clear message instead of silently becoming info; an invalid BLEEPHUB_MAX_WORKFLOWS now logs a warning (value + default used) instead of being silently ignored

findings.finding: The test helper hand-builds a partial `*Server`, producing eight nil-guards in production code and leaving `NewServer` untested
findings.status: fixed — stale premises: `newTestServer` no longer hand-builds a partial server, it goes through the shared `newServerState` constructor exactly as `NewServer` does, and `NewServer` itself is exercised directly (the suite-wide `testServer` is built by `NewServer` in `bleephub_test.go:169`, and `build_info_test.go`/`lifecycle_test.go`/`otel_test.go` call it and drive real handlers). findings.finding: ANSI console logging in production plus 29 stdlib `log` calls that bypass zerolog, the level filter and the telemetry bridge
findings.status: fixed — production logging now defaults to structured JSON, with ANSI console output opt-in via `BLEEPHUB_LOG_FORMAT=console`. Every server-runtime stdlib `log.*` call is gone: store-layer error logging routes through a wired `Store.logger` (the configured zerolog logger; a nop until `NewServer` sets it), and the boot-time package functions (`MustNewPersistence` quorum wait, `AdminToken` requirement) route through the zerolog global logger, which `main.go` points at the same configured logger. The stdlib `log` package is only used by the standalone `internal/emojigen` build-time generator, which has no logging pipeline and correctly stays on it. Regression test asserts store errors emit structured fields

findings.status: fixed — documented /ui/ as a deliberate, explained exception to the route-registry invariant (it cannot join routePatterns without breaking the authz-matrix/api-definition tests)

findings.status: fixed — `securityHeadersMiddleware` wraps the whole handler chain, setting `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy` on every response, `Strict-Transport-Security` over TLS, and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` + a `Content-Security-Policy` for `/ui`; stricter per-endpoint CSPs run after and are not clobbered. Unit-tested

findings.finding: Metrics computed client-side by walking every repo, every run page and every run's jobs, re-run every 3 seconds — one tab self-DoSes the server
findings.status: fixed — `GET /internal/metrics` + `GET /internal/status`, two requests where there were 1 + N repos + every page of their runs + every run's jobs + a runners call per repo. Also removed a duplicate `["metrics"]` query racing itself at 3s against 5s. One honest gap: the server has no total of stored workflow runs (`WorkflowSubmissions` counts something else), so the card is relabelled "Workflow submissions" rather than showing the wrong number under the old label, with a test asserting no card reads "Workflow runs". See WEB-045 for the non-admin consequence and WEB-046 for the remaining fan-out

findings.finding: 19 state-changing controls, including security and destructive ones, have no error handling and never render an error
findings.status: fixed — 23 sites / 28 controls across 10 files, via a shared `useMutationError` + `MutationError` over the existing banner, which gained `role="alert"`. The survey's "19 across 12 pages" was wrong in both directions: it scoped the search to the file rather than the enclosing component. Includes the three hand-rolled ones — both `LoginPage` auth submits left the button spinning forever, and `AppHeader.submitLogout` could skip the logout POST entirely. Verified 0 mutations remain with no `onError`, no rendered error and no `MutationError`

findings.finding: The only dialog primitive, used at 40 sites, has no dialog role, no focus trap, no Escape and leaves the page tabbable
findings.status: fixed at the primitive, so all 40 `<Modal>` usages across 21 files — `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-labelledby`, focus-into-dialog, a Tab/Shift-Tab trap, Escape, and focus restored to the invoking element. Note a mount-order stack is the wrong way to find the topmost dialog: React runs effects child-first, so a nested dialog registers before its parent. Resolved by document order; caught by the stacked-dialog test

findings.finding: The app renders nothing until the session probe resolves, with no timeout; a network error is indistinguishable from signed-out
findings.status: fixed — an explicit `probing`/`signed-in`/`signed-out`/`failed` union in place of a nullable boolean, each rendering distinctly (`role="status"` while probing, `role="alert"` plus a working retry on failure), and the probe bounded by `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`. `/auth/session` always answers 200, so a rejection is genuinely a transport fault and is thrown rather than folded into signed-out

findings.finding: Extends a path outside the repository that does not exist, and nothing references the file — 967 lines of e2e TypeScript never type-checked
findings.status: fixed — it extended a path resolving outside the repository entirely. Repointed and wired into `bun run typecheck`; it surfaced 2 real errors in `web/e2e/webhook-receiver.ts`, fixed by porting the helper to `node:http` rather than adding `@types/bun`, whose globals would leak into the application's own typecheck. All 4 e2e files now type-check; previously zero did

findings.finding: The 13 core test suites never execute and are never type-checked; a further 11 e2e tests are unreachable from any config
findings.status: fixed — the 13 core suites run and type-check after the setup path was made absolute; the 9 `core/e2e` tests are intentionally owned by Playwright under WEB-047 rather than silently claimed by Vitest. The combined app/core Vitest project now executes 485 tests and measures all source files, not only files imported by tests

findings.finding: The dev proxy omits `/auth` and `/settings`, so `bun run dev` cannot authenticate
findings.status: fixed — proxied authentication, settings, Classroom data, and invitation entry points

findings.finding: React state mutated inside a query function, so the 5-second refetch discards every page the user loaded
findings.status: fixed — watchers and forks now use query-owned infinite pagination

findings.finding: "Load more" has no in-flight guard, so two clicks append the same page twice
findings.status: fixed — the request and control share an in-flight guard

findings.finding: Not one fetch accepts or forwards an abort signal, and there is no request timeout anywhere
findings.status: fixed — a module-wide abort controller backs cancellation (sign-out) and per-request abort signals from react-query `queryFn` contexts are threaded through the low-level helpers (`fetchJSON`/`ghFetch`/`ghFetchPage`/`ghFetchEnvelope`/`apiFetch`/`ghGraphQL`), combined via `AbortSignal.any` with the sign-out controller and a 30s default request timeout. The remaining 24 high-level `fetch*` helpers now each accept and forward `signal?: AbortSignal` (including the `Promise.all` fan-outs in `fetchUsers`/`fetchOrgs`), and their 28 `queryFn` call sites across 14 pages thread the query's signal, so a cancelled/unmounted query aborts its in-flight request everywhere; non-query callers (effects, mutations, event handlers) keep the optional param unset and are unaffected. Verified: typecheck, build, all 511 web tests, knip and audit green

findings.finding: A bearer token in localStorage alongside three unsanitised HTML sinks, safe only via an untested server-side coupling
findings.status: fixed — pasted PAT/OAuth credentials are exchanged once at `POST /auth/token` for an opaque HttpOnly browser session and never persisted or read from browser storage; Discussions renders the Markdown source through react-markdown/GFM instead of trusting any `bodyHTML`. Source-invariant tests reject both regressions

findings.finding: 3,552 lines with ten near-identical request helpers and 34 inline fetches, each subtly different
findings.status: fixed — the thirty-four inline fetches collapsed to a single primitive: `apiFetch` (api.ts:183) is the only raw `fetch` in the file, adding the shared abort signal, and everything funnels through it via a small set of *distinct* (not near-identical) typed helpers — `fetchJSON`, `ghFetch`/`ghFetchPage`/`ghFetchEnvelope` for the `/api/v3` list/page/envelope shapes, and `ghSend`/`ghPostJSON` for writes. The only calls that reach `apiFetch` directly rather than through `ghFetch` are the handful of management/OAuth surfaces (`/auth/token` device-token, `/settings/oauth-apps`) whose auth and redirect semantics genuinely differ from `/api/v3`, so they are deliberately not on the GitHub-token path. The remaining "needs generated contracts" gap is closed by WEB-013: the `ghFetch<T>` response types are now `components["schemas"][…]` contracts generated from the vendored OpenAPI description for every core resource

findings.finding: Every response is cast, never validated, against 2,153 hand-written lines with no generator
findings.status: fixed — the generator now exists: `scripts/gen-web-openapi-types.sh` runs `openapi-typescript` (pinned 7.13.0, via `bunx` so it is not a locked dependency and never touches the bundle, `bun audit`, or the dependency-age gate) over the *same* vendored, pinned GitHub OpenAPI description the Go server validates against (`third_party/github-openapi.json.gz`), emitting `third_party/github-openapi.d.ts` (~144k lines, `.d.ts` so `skipLibCheck` skips type-checking it and it erases to zero runtime/bundle). The generated file is a committed *witness* of the vendored spec: `scripts/check-web-openapi-types-drift.sh` (wired into the Web CI job) fails if it is not a byte-for-byte regeneration of the pinned spec, so a spec bump that was not regenerated — or a hand-edit — cannot silently drift the web contract. All vendored artifacts (the spec, its `.VERSION`/route-index, the GraphQL schema, and this generated file) live under `third_party/` with a provenance `README`. Adoption is underway: thirty-one `Github*` types in `types.ts` are now aliases to their `components["schemas"][…]` contracts instead of hand-written projections — `GithubContentFile`, `GithubDeployKey`, `GithubThreadSubscription`, `GithubSSHSigningKey`, `GithubPublicKey`, `GithubTeamMembership`, `GithubGistCommit`, `GithubReleaseAsset`, `GithubDependabotSecret`, `GithubCodespaceMachine`, `GithubDeploymentBranchPolicy`, `GithubCopilotSpaceResource`, `GithubTeamMember`, `GithubDeploymentStatus`, `GithubPackageVersion`, `GithubEnterpriseTeam`, `GithubPendingDeployment`, `GithubIssueType`, `GithubCustomProperty`, `GithubCommunityProfile`, `GithubCodeScanningAnalysis`, `GithubOrgRepoCustomPropertyValues`, `GithubCodeScanningAlertInstance`, `GithubCodeScanningAlert`, `GithubDependabotAlert`, `GithubSecretScanningAlert`, `GithubMilestone`, `GithubDeployment`, `GithubCollaborator`, `GithubCommit`, `GithubIssue` — with every web gate green (typecheck, vitest 511/511, build, knip, jscpd). Two bridge patterns for divergent shapes are established: a per-consumer null-guard (`GithubPendingDeployment` — the spec marks `environment.id` optional, so `DeploymentsPage`/`RunDetailPage` filter it before building `environment_ids`) and a `NonNullable<…>` wrapper where the spec models the whole type nullable (`GithubIssueType`); adopting `GithubCommunityProfile` also let its private nested `GithubCommunityFile` (matched by the spec's `nullable-community-health-file`) be removed. A third decision emerged: where the spec is a *downgrade* — a bare `string` where the UI relies on a narrow union, or dropping a field the UI renders (e.g. `marketplace-account`: `type: string` losing the `"User"`/`"Organization"` union, no `avatar_url`) — the hand-written type is kept by design (also `commit-status` and `copilot-space`, whose spec `state`/role fields widen to bare `string` past the UI's narrow unions). Adopting `code-scanning-alert-instance` (spec makes `location`/`commit_sha` optional, so `CodeScanningPage` optional-chains them) also folded its private nested `GithubCodeScanningAlertLocation` into the generated inline shape. Adopting `dependabot-alert`/`secret-scanning-alert` needed only null-guards for spec-optional fields (`DependabotPage` optional-chains `alert.dependency.package`; `SecretScanningPage` coalesces the optional `number`/`created_at`), and `dependabot-alert` folded away its nested `GithubDependabotAlertPackage`. Kept hand-written as downgrades: `workflow-run`/`check-run` (spec widens `status`/`conclusion` to bare `string` past the `WorkflowStatus`/`GHRunStatus`/`GHConclusion` unions) and `branch-protection` (structural mismatch). `GithubMilestone`/`GithubDeployment`/`GithubCollaborator` adopted cleanly via the `NonNullable<nullable-…>` wrapper. `GithubCommit` adopted the REST `commit` schema (not the git-object `simple-commit` the name-heuristic first tried) with consumers optional-chaining the spec-nullable `commit.author`. `GithubIssue` adopted too, with an IssuesPage `issueLabelPills` normaliser for the spec's `string`-or-object `labels` union and null-guards for optional `assignees`/`body`. The generator keystone and every core GitHub resource are now spec-derived, so the finding (blind casts, no generator) is resolved. The small remainder is hand-written by necessity or design, not by omission: `secret-scanning-location`'s `oneOf` union (openapi-typescript emits members that `Extract` narrows to `never`, so clean adoption would need a `as` cast — which the no-suppression rule forbids) and `hook-delivery` (the generated schema is the full delivery; adopting it needs an item/detail split and request-header shape reconciliation) stay hand-written for structural reasons, and six types are deliberate keep-hand-written downgrades where the spec is less precise than the UI needs (`marketplace-account`, `copilot-space`, `commit-status`, `workflow-run`, `check-run`, `branch-protection`); `Bleephub*`/`Wire*`/`Classroom*` describe bleephub's own API and stay hand-written by design

findings.status: fixed — ci.yml push/pull_request carry a docs-only paths-ignore; any code/config/spec/workflow/ledger change still runs the full pipeline

findings.finding: Account-level public-access blocks disabled to expose one file, and two buckets have no block at all
findings.status: fixed — the startup bucket is now fully private behind CloudFront with an origin access control, the bucket policy grants `s3:GetObject` on the single key to the distribution only, and a `moved` block renames the old policy in place so there is no window without one. The finding's premise was slightly off: `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` is bucket-level, not account-level

findings.finding: AWS-managed keys only, with no rotation or revocation control
findings.status: fixed — a customer-managed key with rotation, a 30-day deletion window and an explicit policy, applied to all three buckets, EFS, all three secrets and the log group, with least-privilege grants on the service roles and CloudFront distribution. Judged warranted: these stores hold every git ref, every artifact, the SSH host key and the admin token, and an AWS-managed key offers no revocation or key-level audit boundary

findings.finding: Public SSH ingress hardcoded with no restriction variable and no IPv6 rule
findings.status: fixed — `ssh_ingress_cidr_blocks`, required with **no default**, validated non-empty, valid IPv4 CIDR, and `/8` or narrower so `0.0.0.0/0` is rejected. Deliberately not "defaulting to something safe": a permissive default is a silent fallback and an empty one a silent no-op

findings.finding: No `prevent_destroy` on any durable resource
findings.status: fixed — `prevent_destroy` on the KMS key, both buckets, EFS and both secrets. It genuinely conflicts with `force_destroy_storage`, and Terraform rejects `prevent_destroy = var.x` outright, so that variable now only empties buckets and the teardown sequence is documented instead of the variable promising something false

findings.finding: Committed build output shipped into the build context, then overwritten
findings.status: fixed — added a per-Dockerfile `Dockerfile.release.dockerignore` (BuildKit honours `<dockerfile>.dockerignore` in preference to the global one, and it *replaces* rather than merges, so it repeats every global rule). Its one addition is `internal/server/dist`: the release image's `builder` stage does `COPY . .` then `COPY --from=ui-builder …/web/dist ./internal/server/dist/` *before* `go build`, so the committed copy shipped into context was pure waste that the fresh build overwrote. Excluding it there is safe (the embed sees the regenerated dist from the ui-builder copy) and worst-case a no-op; the gh-test and shauth images embed the committed dist directly and keep using the global `.dockerignore`, which does not list it. Release-images CI validates the embed

findings.finding: The gate ignores the exit code and decides pass/fail by grepping free text
findings.status: fixed — knip's exit code is the verdict (non-zero past `--max-issues`, default 0); verified it still fails and names the file when the entry point is removed

findings.finding: Disables errexit and matches console wording that upstream is free to change
findings.status: fixed — reads `.statistics.total.clones` from the JSON reporter, because jscpd exits 0 even with 499 clones. Also `--ignore-pattern` was the wrong flag (it takes regexes for code blocks inside files), so `src/__tests__/**` matched nothing and every test file had been scanned

findings.finding: Three jobs perform a cold dependency install while the Go jobs and the Dockerfile cache correctly
findings.status: fixed — the web/browser/shauth-sso jobs cache ~/.bun/install/cache keyed on bun.lock, matching the Go jobs and Dockerfile

findings.finding: The server suite runs 437s against an 8m timeout — 9% headroom, and a slower runner turns it into a failure that reads as a hang
findings.status: fixed

findings.finding: The Trivy image scan is reporting-only; set a blocking severity threshold once the first runs establish the real finding count
findings.status: fixed — pull requests build and load both the release and runner images, then block on every fixed HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability; the images are currently clean

findings.finding: The git and object buckets had no public-access block at all, no TLS-only bucket policy, and no incomplete-multipart-upload cleanup on the two buckets that take pack and artifact uploads; the startup bucket had no encryption configuration
findings.status: fixed — all four blocks on for all three buckets, `Deny` on `aws:SecureTransport = false`, a 7-day abort rule, versioning, and CMK encryption on startup

findings.finding: The only test of the deployment module asserted the **opposite** of correct `desired_count` behaviour — it required Terraform to reconcile the wake controller's out-of-band scaling, which is exactly the bug that terminates a live service — and ran an unguarded `destroy`
findings.status: fixed — the drift check now requires a clean plan and the teardown asserts the `prevent_destroy` guard fires before releasing the six guarded addresses

findings.finding: `aws_efs_file_system.kms_key_id` is ForceNew, so introducing the customer-managed key stops an already-deployed plan on `prevent_destroy` rather than replacing the filesystem. That is the correct failure mode, but a deployed environment needs either the documented AWS Backup restore migration or the key dropped from EFS specifically — an owner decision, not a code one
findings.status: open

findings.finding: Keyless signing relied only on cosign's two internal Rekor POST attempts, so two consecutive main releases built and published every image but stopped before attestation, scanning, and retention when Rekor remained temporarily unavailable
findings.status: fixed as scoped — signing and attestation each use the tested retry helper for five bounded attempts with exponential backoff, while a persistent error still fails the release loudly. The next release proved the failure was deterministic rather than transient and is tracked as CI-063

findings.finding: The 20,849,186-byte release SPDX document was embedded in a Rekor attestation even though the public instance has a 100 KB attestation limit, so all five retries must fail and every main release stops after publishing its image
findings.status: fixed — attach the complete SPDX document to its image as a content-addressed OCI referrer, keylessly sign that SBOM artifact, and attest only its immutable URI and SHA-256 from the image; the bounded size assertion prevents a reference predicate from silently exceeding Rekor's limit

findings.finding: Dependency updates had no quarantine, several analyzer graphs were resolved at execution time, actions and base images used mutable references, and fixed HIGH/CRITICAL findings did not block pull requests
findings.status: fixed — every Go, Bun, Python, NuGet, Terraform, Docker, GitHub Action, Actions Runner and .NET SDK resolution is immutable or content-hashed and must be at least 24 hours old; product and analyzer Go toolchains are pinned to patched 1.25.12 and 1.26.5 releases; analyzer graphs are lockfile-backed; CodeQL, gosec, govulncheck, Semgrep, staticcheck, Trivy, actionlint, shellcheck, knip and duplication checks gate CI; both release images and the rebuilt runner image block on fixed HIGH/CRITICAL findings

findings.finding: GitHub's independent CodeQL policy check could pass before the workflow uploaded its findings, leaving four open log-injection alerts and ten JavaScript quality findings on a completely green pull request
findings.status: fixed — every request-derived repository log field and propagated error crosses a tested CR/LF-safe boundary; nine dead TypeScript symbols and the startup page's executable `document.write` handoff were removed; and the CodeQL workflow now parses its generated SARIF synchronously and fails closed on a finding, missing output or malformed output before its own required job can pass

findings.finding: A single flat package of 406 files and 181k lines. Splitting it is a real improvement but would conflict with every other change here and is an architectural decision to take on its own
findings.status: deferred by decision
